claims.statement: The winged cat, a feline with wings like a bird, bat or other flying creature, is a theme in art and legend going back to prehistory, especially mythological depictions of big cats with eagle wings in Eurasia and North Africa.
claims.statement_id: Kucing bersayap, yaitu felid dengan sayap seperti burung, kelelawar, atau makhluk terbang lain, adalah tema seni dan legenda sejak prasejarah, terutama gambaran mitologis kucing besar bersayap elang di Eurasia dan Afrika Utara.
claims.quote: The winged cat – a feline with wings like a bird, bat or other flying creature – is a theme in artwork and legend going back to prehistory, especially mythological depictions of big cats with eagle wings in Eurasia and North Africa.

claims.statement: Winged pantherines, especially winged lions, are a common theme in the ancient religious and mythological art of the Sumerians and other Mesopotamians, Akkadians, Persians and Scythians.
claims.statement_id: Pantherin bersayap, terutama singa bersayap, adalah tema umum dalam seni religius dan mitologis kuno bangsa Sumeria dan Mesopotamia lain, Akkadia, Persia, dan Skithia.
claims.quote: Pantherines with wings, especially winged lions, are a common theme in ancient religious and mythological art of the Sumerians and other Mesopotamians, Akkadians, Persians, and Scythians

claims.statement: Aq Bars is a legendary winged snow leopard, a symbol of ancient Turkic and Bulgar origin going back to an uncertain pre-literate period.
claims.statement_id: Aq Bars adalah macan tutul salju bersayap yang legendaris, lambang berasal Turkic dan Bulgar kuno, yang berakar pada masa tak pasti sebelum tulisan.
claims.quote: Aq Bars is a legendary winged snow leopard, a symbol of ancient Turkic and Bulgar origin, and going back to an uncertain period in pre-literate history.

claims.statement: In the Book of Daniel, the first beast in the vision of the beasts from the sea (chapter 7) resembled a winged lion.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kitab Daniel, binatang pertama dalam penglihatan tentang binatang-binatang dari laut (pasal 7) menyerupai singa bersayap.
claims.quote: In the Book of Daniel of the Hebrew Bible and Christian Old Testament, the first beast in the vision of the beasts from the sea (chapter 7, dating to around the 2nd century BC) resembled a winged lion.

claims.statement: In medieval Christianity, domestic cats and bats were associated with the Devil, and demons were sometimes depicted as bat-winged cats.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kekristenan abad pertengahan, kucing domestik dan kelelawar dikaitkan dengan Iblis, dan setan kadang digambarkan sebagai kucing bersayap kelelawar.
claims.quote: In later, medieval Christianity, both cats (of the domestic sort) and bats were associated with the Devil, and demons were sometimes depicted as bat-winged cats.

claims.statement: Belief in domestic cats with wings persists to the present day as an urban legend.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan akan kucing domestik bersayap bertahan hingga kini sebagai legenda urban.
claims.quote: Belief in domestic cats with wings persists to the present day as an urban legend.

claims.statement: Sightings of supposedly winged cats are easily explained by medical conditions such as matted hair, loose skin or supernumerary limbs on or near the shoulders that flap like wings as the cat runs.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan kucing yang konon bersayap mudah dijelaskan oleh kondisi medis: rambut kusut, kulit longgar, atau anggota tubuh tambahan di dekat bahu yang mengepak seperti sayap saat kucing berlari.
claims.quote: Sightings of cats with supposed wings are easily explained by medical conditions that can result in matted hair, loose skin, or supernumerary limbs on or near the shoulders, that flap about in a wing-like manner as the cat runs.

claims.statement: There is no evidence of actual bird-like or bat-like wings on cats, and no scientific reason to believe such a thing is possible.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada bukti sayap sungguhan seperti sayap burung atau kelelawar pada kucing, dan tidak ada alasan ilmiah untuk percaya hal itu mungkin.
claims.quote: There is no evidence of actual bird- or bat-like wings, and there is no scientific reason to believe such a thing is possible.

claims.statement: The earliest currently known report of a winged cat is from Henry David Thoreau.
claims.statement_id: Laporan tertua yang kini diketahui tentang kucing bersayap berasal dari Henry David Thoreau.
claims.quote: The earliest currently known report of a winged cat is from Henry David Thoreau:

claims.statement: Thoreau records calling to see the cat in June 1842, when she had gone hunting in the woods as was her wont.
claims.statement_id: Thoreau mencatat kunjungannya pada Juni 1842 untuk melihat kucing itu, yang saat itu sedang berburu di hutan seperti kebiasaannya.
claims.quote: When I called to see her in June, 1842, she was gone a-hunting in the woods, as was her wont

claims.statement: According to the owner, in winter the fur grew thick and flattened along her sides, forming stripes ten or twelve inches long by two and a half wide.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penuturan pemilik, pada musim dingin bulunya menebal dan memipih di sisi tubuhnya, membentuk jalur sepanjang sepuluh atau dua belas inci dan lebar dua setengah inci.
claims.quote: that in the winter the fur grew thick and flatted out along her sides, forming stripes ten or twelve inches long by two and a half wide

claims.statement: Some people thought the cat was partly a flying squirrel or some other wild animal.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang mengira kucing itu sebagian tupai terbang atau hewan liar lain.
claims.quote: Some thought it was part flying-squirrel or some other wild animal, which is not impossible

claims.statement: The Japanese-language article records that in 1826 an animal with a cat's face and wings (翼) was captured in Oshika village, Ado district, Suruga province, Japan.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jepang mencatat bahwa pada 1826 di desa Oshika, Distrik Ado, Provinsi Suruga, Jepang, ditangkap hewan berwajah kucing yang bersayap (翼).
claims.quote: 1826年、日本の駿河国有渡郡小鹿村にて、顔が猫で翼の生えた動物が捕獲される

claims.statement: In the imaginary realm winged cats (chats ailés) also appear, generally with true wings, such as the cats of the Norse goddess Freyja.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ranah imajiner juga ada kucing bersayap (chats ailés), umumnya bersayap sungguhan, seperti kucing-kucing milik dewi Nordik Freyja.
claims.quote: Dans le domaine imaginaire, des chats ailés sont également présents, bien qu'en général pourvus d'ailes véritables, tels les chats de la déesse nordique Freyja.

claims.statement: Catwings is a 1988–1999 series of children's picture books by Ursula K. Le Guin featuring several winged cats.
claims.statement_id: Catwings adalah serangkaian buku bergambar anak 1988–1999 karya Ursula K. Le Guin yang menampilkan beberapa kucing bersayap.
claims.quote: Catwings, a 1988–1999 series of children's picture books by Ursula K. Le Guin, features several winged cats.

claims.statement: In the Kongo language, Abada refers to a mythical animal similar to a unicorn, but it has two crooked horns rather than the unicorn's single one.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Kongo, Abada menunjuk hewan mitos yang mirip unicorn, tetapi memiliki dua tanduk bengkok, bukan satu tanduk seperti unicorn.
claims.quote: In the Kongo language, Abada refers to a mythical animal similar to a unicorn. The Abada, however, has two crooked horns as opposed to a unicorn's single one.

claims.statement: The Abada's horns hang limp and soft when it is relaxed or sleeping, but harden when it feels threatened.
claims.statement_id: Tanduk Abada terkulai lunak saat ia santai atau tidur, tetapi mengeras ketika ia merasa terancam.
claims.quote: The Abada's horns hang limp and soft when it is relaxed or sleeping, but hardens when it feels threatened.

claims.statement: The Abada's horns can act as an antidote to poison and disease.
claims.statement_id: Tanduk Abada dapat berfungsi sebagai penawar racun dan penyakit.
claims.quote: The Abada's horns can act as an antidote to poison and disease.

claims.statement: The Abada has been described as the size of a small donkey with the tail of a boar.
claims.statement_id: Abada digambarkan seukuran keledai kecil dengan ekor seperti babi hutan.
claims.quote: It has been described as being the size of a small donkey with the tail of a boar.

claims.statement: Its arrival is viewed as a sign of good fortune and a supernatural source of hope.
claims.statement_id: Kedatangannya dipandang sebagai pertanda keberuntungan dan sumber harapan supernatural.
claims.quote: Its arrival is viewed as a sign of good fortune and a supernatural source of hope.

claims.statement: The Abada is also known as Nillekma or Arase.
claims.statement_id: Abada juga dikenal sebagai Nillekma atau Arase.
claims.quote: The Abada is also known as Nillekma or Arase.

claims.statement: The word was first used for a unicorn-like creature in the 17th century by the Capuchin missionary Giovani Antonio Cavazzi da Montecucco.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini pertama kali dipakai untuk menyebut makhluk mirip unicorn pada abad ke-17 melalui misionaris Kapusin Giovani Antonio Cavazzi da Montecucco.
claims.quote: Although it was first used to describe a unicorn-like creature in the 17th century via the Capuchin missionary Giovani Antonio Cavazzi da Montecucco

claims.statement: Gould says this creature is indigenous to Kordofan and, according to Cavassi, known in Congo under another name (Abada).
claims.statement_id: Gould menyebut makhluk ini berasal dari Kordofan, dan menurut Cavassi dikenal di Kongo dengan nama lain (Abada).
claims.quote: as indigenous to Kordofan, and, by Cavassi, as known in Congo under that of

claims.statement: Gould quotes an animal seller's description of a creature the size of a small donkey with a thick body, thin bones, coarse hair and a boar-like tail; its long forehead horn hangs when it is alone but is raised at once on seeing an enemy.
claims.statement_id: Gould mengutip pengakuan seorang penjual hewan tentang makhluk seukuran keledai kecil dengan badan tebal, tulang tipis, rambut kasar, dan ekor seperti babi hutan; tanduk panjang di dahinya dibiarkan terkulai saat sendirian tetapi ditegakkan seketika saat melihat musuh.
claims.quote: It is the size of a small donkey, has a thick body and thin bones, coarse hair, and tail like a boar. It has a long horn on its forehead, and lets it hang when alone, but erects it immediately on seeing an enemy.

claims.statement: The passage quoted from Father Tellez says the unicorn is not to be confounded with the abada, a matter they usually dispute.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan dari Bapa Tellez menyatakan unicorn tidak boleh dikacaukan dengan abada, yang sering diperdebatkan.
claims.quote: that the unicorn is not to be confounded with the abada, about which they usually dispute

claims.statement: The abada has two crooked horns, not as sovereign as the unicorn's, though they serve as antidotes against poison.
claims.statement_id: Abada memiliki dua tanduk bengkok yang tidak seampuh tanduk unicorn, tetapi berfungsi sebagai penawar racun.
claims.quote: the abada has two crooked horns, which are not so sovereign, although they will serve as antidotes against poison.

claims.statement: The statement comes from a Portuguese who had lived some time in Abyssinia, quoted by Father Tellez.
claims.statement_id: Pernyataan itu berasal dari seorang Portugis yang pernah tinggal beberapa waktu di Abisinia, dikutip oleh Bapa Tellez.
claims.quote: a Portuguese who had lived some time in Abyssinia, and is quoted by Father Tellez

claims.statement: The second article describes the abada, also called nillekma or arase, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as a unicorn-like mythological animal that differs in having two horns (due corna) instead of one.
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menyebut abada, juga disebut nillekma atau arase, di Republik Demokratik Kongo sebagai hewan mitologis mirip unicorn yang berbeda karena memiliki dua tanduk (due corna), bukan satu.
claims.quote: L'abada, detto anche nillekma o arase, nella Repubblica Democratica del Congo, è un animale mitologico simile ad un unicorno: l'unica differenza è che l'abada possiede due corna, mentre l'unicorno una sola.

claims.statement: It is said to be native to Kordofan, a central province of Sudan.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia berasal dari Kordofan, sebuah provinsi di bagian tengah Sudan.
claims.quote: Si dice sia nativo del Kordofan, una provincia centrale del Sudan.

claims.statement: The third article says the abada differs from the unicorn in having two curved horns (dois chifres curvados) and that its horns can serve as an antidote to poison.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ketiga menyatakan abada berbeda dari unicorn karena punya dua tanduk melengkung (dois chifres curvados) dan tanduknya dapat menjadi penawar racun.
claims.quote: O abada difere do unicórnio por ter dois chifres curvados. Os chifres do abada podem servir como um antídoto para veneno.

claims.statement: A kishi (plural: makishi) is a man-eating, many-headed creature with long, tangled hair falling over its face, recorded in the folklore of the Ambundu people in Angola.
claims.statement_id: Kishi (jamak: makishi) adalah makhluk pemakan manusia berkepala banyak dengan rambut panjang kusut yang menutupi wajahnya, tercatat dalam cerita rakyat orang Ambundu di Angola.
claims.quote: A kishi (plural: makishi) is a man-eating, many-headed creature with long, tangled hair that falls over its face, recorded in the folklore of the Ambundu people in Angola.

claims.statement: According to one legend, there was a kishi chief who could regrow his head as soon as it was cut off.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu legenda, ada seorang kepala kishi yang mampu menumbuhkan kembali kepalanya begitu kepala itu dipenggal.
claims.quote: According to one legend, there was a kishi chief who had the ability to regrow his head as soon as it is cut off.

claims.statement: Makishi appear in the legend of Sudika-mbambi, where they destroyed Kimanaueze's village and massacred the people.
claims.statement_id: Makishi muncul dalam legenda Sudika-mbambi, tempat mereka menghancurkan desa Kimanaueze dan membantai penduduknya.
claims.quote: Makishi appear in the legend of Sudika-mbambi, where they destroyed Kimanaueze's village and massacred the people.

claims.statement: The word kishi, nkishi or mukisi means spirit in several Bantu languages.
claims.statement_id: Kata kishi, nkishi, atau mukisi berarti roh (spirit) dalam beberapa bahasa Bantu.
claims.quote: The word kishi, nkishi, or mukisi means "spirit" in several Bantu languages

claims.statement: The second article calls the kishi a two-faced demon (demone) of Angolan mythology: a handsome man's face on the front of its body and a hyena's face (iena) on the back.
claims.statement_id: Artikel kedua menyebut kishi sebagai iblis (demone) bermuka dua dalam mitologi Angola: di bagian depan tubuhnya ada wajah lelaki tampan dan di bagian belakang wajah hiena (iena).
claims.quote: Il kishi è un demone a due volti della mitologia angolana. Secondo la leggenda, un kishi ha il volto di un uomo umano attraente sulla parte anteriore del corpo e quello di una iena sulla parte posteriore.

claims.statement: Kishi are said to use their human face to speak and to attract young women (giovani donne), whom they then eat with the hyena face.
claims.statement_id: Konon kishi memakai wajah manusianya untuk berbicara dan memikat perempuan muda (giovani donne), yang kemudian dimakannya dengan wajah hienanya.
claims.quote: Si dice che i kishi usino il loro volto umano, oltre che per parlare e per attrarre delle giovani donne, che poi mangiano con il volto di iena.

claims.statement: The hyena face is said to have long sharp teeth and jaws (mascelle) so strong they cannot be pulled off whatever it bites.
claims.statement_id: Wajah hiena itu konon bergigi panjang dan tajam dengan rahang (mascelle) yang begitu kuat sehingga tak dapat dilepaskan dari apa yang digigitnya.
claims.quote: Si dice che la faccia della iena abbia lunghi denti affilati e mascelle così forti da non poter essere staccate da ciò che morde.

claims.statement: Werner writes that the makishi of the Ambundu in Angola play the same part in folk-tales as the amazimu.
claims.statement_id: Werner menulis bahwa makishi orang Ambundu di Angola memainkan peran yang sama dalam cerita rakyat seperti amazimu (raksasa pemakan manusia).
claims.quote: The makishi of the Ambundu in Angola play the same part in folk-tales as the amazimu

claims.statement: According to Werner, their name may perhaps be connected with the Kongo word nkishi (nkisi in some dialects).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Werner, nama mereka mungkin berhubungan dengan kata Kongo nkishi (nkisi dalam beberapa dialek).
claims.quote: their name may perhaps be connected with the Kongo nkishi (nkisi in some dialects), which meant originally

claims.statement: In the tale of Sudika-Mbambi, while he was gone, cannibal monsters called makishi descended on the village and sacked it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Sudika-Mbambi, ketika seorang anak desa pergi, monster kanibal yang disebut makishi menyerbu desa dan menjarahnya.
claims.quote: While he was gone certain cannibal monsters, called makishi, descended on the village and sacked it

claims.statement: The makishi are sometimes said to have many heads.
claims.statement_id: Makishi kadang dikatakan berkepala banyak.
claims.quote: The makishi are sometimes said to have many heads

claims.statement: Chatelain records the plural Ma-kishi and the singular Di-kishi or Kishi.
claims.statement_id: Chatelain mencatat bentuk jamak Ma-kishi dan bentuk tunggal Di-kishi atau Kishi.
claims.quote: Compare this account of the Ma-kishi (singular Di-kishi, or Kishi) with those given in the Ma-kishi stories

claims.statement: According to Chatelain, the long hair and the many heads of some Ma-kishi are the only points in which the Ma-kishi of the A-mbundu differ from their descriptions of the A-tua.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Chatelain, rambut panjang dan banyak kepala pada sebagian Ma-kishi adalah satu-satunya hal yang membedakan Ma-kishi orang A-mbundu dari gambaran mereka tentang A-tua.
claims.quote: This long hair, and the many heads of some Ma-kishi, are the only points in which the Ma-kishi of the A-mbundu disagree with their descriptions of the A-tua

claims.statement: Chatelain mentions long, tangled hair and the faculty of growing another head as soon as one is cut off, which he had not heard of in any pygmy tribe.
claims.statement_id: Chatelain menyebut ciri rambut panjang kusut dan kemampuan menumbuhkan kepala lain begitu satu kepala dipenggal, yang tidak ia temukan pada suku pigmi (pygmy) mana pun.
claims.quote: But, though I have not heard of any pygmy tribe wearing long, tangled hair, or having the faculty of growing another head as soon as one is cut off

claims.statement: In one tale the Di-kishi husband evidently has more than one head, as he wants the woman to give him two-headed children.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu cerita, suami Di-kishi jelas berkepala lebih dari satu karena ia ingin perempuan itu melahirkan anak berkepala dua.
claims.quote: husband has evidently more than one head, as he wants the woman to give him two-headed children.

claims.statement: Ọba (known as Obá in Latin America) is the orisha of the River Oba, whose source lies near Igbon, where her worship originates.
claims.statement_id: Ọba (dikenal sebagai Obá di Amerika Latin) adalah orisha sungai Oba (River Oba); hulu sungai itu dekat Igbon, tempat pemujaannya berasal.
claims.quote: (known as Obá in Latin America) is the orisha of the River Oba, the source of which lies near Igbon, where her worship originates.

claims.statement: During the wars of the 19th century her centers of worship moved to the more secure town of Ogbomosho.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa perang abad ke-19, pusat pemujaannya pindah ke kota Ogbomosho yang lebih aman.
claims.quote: During the wars of the 19th century, her centers of worship moved to the more secure town Ogbomosho.

claims.statement: She is traditionally identified as the senior wife of Shango.
claims.statement_id: Secara tradisional ia dikenal sebagai istri senior (senior wife) Shango.
claims.quote: She is traditionally identified as the senior wife of Shango

claims.statement: She represents stability and sacred bonds and is syncretized with Saint Catherine of Siena.
claims.statement_id: Ia melambangkan kestabilan dan ikatan suci, dan disinkretiskan dengan Santa Katarina dari Siena (Saint Catherine of Siena).
claims.quote: She represents stability and sacred bonds. She is syncretized with Saint Catherine of Siena.

claims.statement: The most popular myth in West Africa, Brazil and Cuba has Oba cut off her ear to serve to her husband Shango as food, because a co-wife (most often Oshun) convinced her it would secure Shango's attention.
claims.statement_id: Mitos paling populer di Afrika Barat, Brasil, dan Kuba (West Africa, Brazil, Cuba) menceritakan Oba memotong telinganya untuk disajikan sebagai makanan bagi suaminya Shango, karena seorang madunya (paling sering Oshun) meyakinkannya bahwa itu akan menarik perhatian Shango.
claims.quote: the most popular myth found in West Africa, Brazil, and Cuba has Oba cutting off her ear to serve to her husband Shango as food, because one of her co-wives (most often Oshun) has convinced her this will secure Shango's attention.

claims.statement: Once Shango sees the ear and realizes Oba has mutilated herself, he chases her from his house into permanent exile.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Shango melihat telinga itu dan sadar Oba melukai dirinya sendiri, ia mengusir Oba dari rumahnya ke pengasingan permanen.
claims.quote: Once Shango sees the ear and realizes Oba has mutilated herself, he chases her from his house and into permanent exile.

claims.statement: Bascom notes that though the story is known in many parts of Yoruba country, her priest in Ogbomosho did not recognize it.
claims.statement_id: Bascom mencatat bahwa kisah ini dikenal di banyak bagian negeri Yoruba, tetapi tidak diakui oleh pendetanya di Ogbomosho.
claims.quote: Bascom notes that though this story is known in many parts of Yoruba country, it was not recognized by her priest in Ogbomosho.

claims.statement: There are a few variations of the myth in Cuba where Oya rather than Oshun tricks Oba.
claims.statement_id: Ada beberapa variasi mitos di Kuba ketika Oya, bukan Oshun, yang menipu Oba.
claims.quote: There are a few variations of the myth in Cuba where Oya rather than Oshun tricks Oba.

claims.statement: In the verses of the Odu Ifá, Oba lends her ear on the advice of Ifá and this successfully ties Shango to Oba.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ayat-ayat Odu Ifá, Oba meminjamkan telinganya atas nasihat Ifá, dan langkah itu berhasil mengikat Shango kepada Oba.
claims.quote: in the verses of the Odu Ifá, Oba lends her ear at the advice of Ifá and the measure successfully ties Shango to Oba

claims.statement: Grieving, she became the Oba river, which intersects with the Oshun river.
claims.statement_id: Dalam duka, ia menjadi sungai Oba (Oba river) yang bersilangan dengan sungai Oshun.
claims.quote: Grieving, she became the Oba river which intersects with the Oshun river

claims.statement: González-Wippler describes her as the daughter of Yemoja and one of the consorts of Shango.
claims.statement_id: González-Wippler menggambarkannya sebagai putri Yemoja dan salah satu pasangan Shango.
claims.quote: describes her as the daughter of Yemoja and one of the consorts of Shango

claims.statement: Obba is an orisha (Orisha) who represents repressed love (amor reprimido), sacrifice for a loved one, suffering, and marital fidelity (fidelidad conyugal).
claims.statement_id: Obba adalah seorang orisha (Orisha) yang melambangkan cinta yang terpendam (amor reprimido), pengorbanan bagi orang yang dicintai, penderitaan, dan kesetiaan suami-istri (fidelidad conyugal).
claims.quote: Obba es una Orisha y representa el amor reprimido y el sacrificio por el ser que uno ama, el sufrimiento y simboliza la fidelidad conyugal.

claims.statement: She is associated with lakes and lagoons (lagos, lagunas).
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan danau dan laguna (lagos, lagunas).
claims.quote: Está relacionada con los lagos y las lagunas.

claims.statement: Together with Oyá and Yewá she dwells in cemeteries (cementerios), and they represent fearless women warriors (guerreras temerarias).
claims.statement_id: Bersama Oyá dan Yewá ia berdiam di pemakaman (cementerios), dan mereka melambangkan para pejuang perempuan yang berani (guerreras temerarias).
claims.quote: Junto con Oyá y Yewá habita en los cementerios y representan a guerreras temerarias.

claims.statement: Her name comes from Yorùbá Òbbá (Òbè: soup, sopa; Obá: king, rey), literally "she of the king's soup" (La de la sopa del rey).
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari kata Yorùbá Òbbá (Òbè: sup, sopa; Obá: raja, rey), secara harfiah "dia yang memegang sup raja" (La de la sopa del rey).
claims.quote: Su nombre proviene del Yorùbá Òbbá (Òbè: sopa - Obá: rey), literalmente "La de la sopa del rey".

claims.statement: She is female, strong, feared and energetic, considered stronger than many male orishas (Orishas masculinos); the only one who defeated her in battle was Oggun.
claims.statement_id: Ia perempuan, kuat, ditakuti, dan energik, dianggap lebih kuat daripada banyak orisha laki-laki (Orishas masculinos); satu-satunya yang berhasil mengalahkannya dalam pertempuran adalah Oggun.
claims.quote: Femenina, fuerte, temida, enérgica, considerada más fuerte que muchos Orishas masculinos. El único que logró derrotarla en batalla fue Oggun.

claims.statement: Out of shame the orisha ran to her father Obbatalá and wept so much that her tears (lágrimas) created rivers and lagoons (ríos y lagunas).
claims.statement_id: Karena malu, sang orisha lari kepada ayahnya Obbatalá dan menangis begitu banyak hingga air matanya (lágrimas) menciptakan sungai dan laguna (ríos y lagunas).
claims.quote: y la orisha, por vergüenza, corrió donde su padre Obbatalá, y en eso, lloró tanto, que creó ríos y lagunas con sus lágrimas

claims.statement: Ayao is an orisha in the Santería pantheon; she is the orisha of the air and is considered to reside in the forest and in the eye of the tornado.
claims.statement_id: Ayao adalah orisha dalam panteon Santería; ia orisha udara (air) dan dianggap berdiam di hutan (forest) serta di mata tornado.
claims.quote: Ayao is an orisha in the Santería pantheon. She is the orisha of the air, and is considered to reside in both the forest and in the eye of the tornado.

claims.statement: She works closely with Ọsanyìn and is a fierce warrior.
claims.statement_id: Ia bekerja erat dengan Ọsanyìn dan merupakan pejuang yang garang (fierce warrior).
claims.quote: She works closely with Ọsanyìn and is a fierce warrior.

claims.statement: Ayao's implements include a crossbow with a serpent, a quill and nine stones.
claims.statement_id: Di antara perlengkapan Ayao terdapat busur silang dengan ular (crossbow with a serpent), sebatang bulu pena, dan sembilan batu.
claims.quote: Ayao has among her implements a crossbow with a serpent, a quill, and nine stones.

claims.statement: She is commonly placed next to her sister Oya; her colors are brown and green.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya ditempatkan di samping saudarinya, Oya; warnanya cokelat dan hijau (brown and green).
claims.quote: She is commonly placed next to her sister, Oya. Her colors are brown and green.

claims.statement: Ayao's cult was thought to be lost among adherents, but a growing number of olorichas have her in their possession.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Ayao sempat dianggap hilang di kalangan penganut, tetapi semakin banyak olorichas yang memilikinya (have her in their possession).
claims.quote: Ayao's cult was thought to be lost among various adherents; however, a growing number of olorichas have her in their possession.

claims.statement: Aiaó (in Castilian: Ayaó) is an orixá of the Lucumi/Santeria pantheon.
claims.statement_id: Aiaó (dalam bahasa Kastila: Ayaó) adalah seorang orixá dalam panteon Lucumi/Santeria.
claims.quote: Aiaó (em castelhano: Ayaó) é uma orixá do panteão Lucumi/Santeria.

claims.statement: Aiaó's cult was thought lost among followers (sectários), but a growing number of initiates (iniciados) receive her during possessions (possessões).
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Aiaó dikira telah hilang di antara para penganut (sectários), tetapi makin banyak inisiat (iniciados) menerimanya dalam kerasukan (possessões).
claims.quote: Pensava-se que o culto a Aiaó tivesse se perdido entre os sectários. Mas um crescente número de iniciados recebem-na durante as possessões.

claims.statement: Some individuals take the bow and arrow (arco e flecha) from Oiá's crown and place it in Aiaó's receptacle (receptáulo).
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang mengambil busur dan panah (arco e flecha) dari mahkota Oiá dan menaruhnya di wadah (receptáulo) Aiaó.
claims.quote: Alguns indivíduos retiram o arco e flecha da coroa de Oiá e colocam no receptáulo de Aiaó.

claims.statement: She usually appears beside her sister (irmã) Oiá; her colors are brown (marrom) and green (verde).
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya muncul di samping saudarinya (irmã), Oiá; warnanya cokelat (marrom) dan hijau (verde).
claims.quote: Ela aparece em geral ao lado da irmã, Oiá ou na abóboda; as cores são marrom e verde.

claims.statement: Ayao is an oriša (božstvo, deity) in the pantheon of the Caribbean (karibského) religion Santería; she is the oriša of the air (vzduchu).
claims.statement_id: Ayao adalah oriša (božstvo, dewa) dalam panteon agama Karibia (karibského) Santería; ia oriša udara (vzduchu).
claims.quote: Ayao je oriša (božstvo) v panteonu karibského nábožensrtví Santería. Je orišou vzduchu.

claims.statement: Ayao dwells in the forest (lese) and in the eye of the tornado (oku tornáda).
claims.statement_id: Ayao berdiam di hutan (lese) dan di mata tornado (oku tornáda).
claims.quote: Ayao pobývá v lese a v oku tornáda.

claims.statement: In Yoruba mythology, Egbere are malevolent humanoid supernatural beings believed to live in the woods and to be active only at night.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Yoruba, Egbere adalah sejenis makhluk gaib mirip manusia yang jahat (malevolent humanoid), dipercaya tinggal di hutan (woods) dan hanya aktif pada malam hari.
claims.quote: In Yoruba mythology, Egbere are a type of malevolent humanoid supernatural being believed to reside in the woods and active only at night.

claims.statement: Oxford's A Dictionary of the Yoruba language defines Egbere as a Yoruba word for fairy or goblin.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Yoruba terbitan Oxford (A Dictionary of the Yoruba language) mendefinisikan Egbere sebagai kata Yoruba untuk peri atau goblin (fairy or goblin).
claims.quote: Oxford's A Dictionary of the Yoruba language defines Egbere as a Yoruba word for fairy or goblin.

claims.statement: According to William Taylor's 1898 account, written in a colonial and often condescending tone, Egbere inhabit graves.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan William Taylor tahun 1898, yang ditulis dengan nada kolonial dan sering merendahkan, Egbere menghuni kuburan (graves).
claims.quote: According to William Taylor's 1898 account, written in a colonial and often condescending tone, Egbere inhabit graves.

claims.statement: Egbere are described as short in stature.
claims.statement_id: Egbere digambarkan bertubuh pendek (short in stature).
claims.quote: Egbere are described as being short in stature

claims.statement: Egbere are associated with a small mat; it is believed that whoever takes the mat of wealth from an Egbere will attain unimaginable riches.
claims.statement_id: Egbere dikaitkan dengan sehelai tikar kecil (small mat); ada kepercayaan bahwa siapa pun yang berhasil merebut tikar kekayaan (mat of wealth) dari Egbere akan memperoleh kekayaan tak terbayangkan.
claims.quote: are associated with a small mat. There is a belief that anyone who manages to take the mat of wealth from an Egbere will attain unimaginable riches.

claims.statement: They are said to cry constantly, though the sincerity of these tears is questionable.
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon terus-menerus menangis (constantly cry), meskipun ketulusan air mata itu diragukan.
claims.quote: They are said to constantly cry, though the sincerity of these tears is questionable.

claims.statement: There are spirits called Egbere, who are said to exert an evil influence in the world.
claims.statement_id: Ada roh (spirits) yang disebut Egbere, yang konon memberi pengaruh jahat (evil influence) di dunia.
claims.quote: There are spirits called Egbere, who are said to exert an evil influence in the world.

claims.statement: Locals declare these spirits can be seen, leaving the graves they inhabit at midnight and returning before daybreak.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penduduk setempat, roh-roh ini dapat dilihat; mereka meninggalkan kuburan yang mereka huni pada tengah malam (midnight) dan kembali sebelum fajar (daybreak).
claims.quote: The native declares these spirits can be seen, and that they leave graves they inhabit at midnight, to return to them before daybreak.

claims.statement: It is whispered that riding sheep is the delight of the Egbere and that they cause sheep to perish from disease.
claims.statement_id: Dibisikkan bahwa menunggangi domba (sheep riding) adalah kegemaran Egbere, dan mereka menjadi penyebab domba binasa karena penyakit (disease).
claims.quote: It is whispered that sheep riding is the delight of the Egbere, and that they are the cause of the destruction of sheep by disease.

claims.statement: The medicine man is often called to drive them away or to supply a charm or fetich as protection.
claims.statement_id: Dukun (medicine man) sering dipanggil untuk mengusir mereka atau memberikan jimat (charm or fetich) sebagai pelindung.
claims.quote: The medicine man is often called to drive them away, or to supply a charm or fetich as a protection.

claims.statement: Mbwiri is a Central African demon said to possess people; those he possesses would usually be diagnosed with epilepsy by a doctor.
claims.statement_id: Mbwiri adalah iblis (demon) dari Afrika Tengah yang konon merasuki orang; orang yang dirasukinya biasanya akan didiagnosis dokter menderita epilepsi.
claims.quote: Mbwiri is a Central African demon who is said to possess people. Those he possesses would usually be diagnosed with epilepsy by a doctor.

claims.statement: Mbwiri is said to abhor good living, and this is the best way to drive him out.
claims.statement_id: Mbwiri konon membenci hidup enak (good living), dan karena itu cara ini dianggap terbaik untuk mengusirnya.
claims.quote: Mbwiri is said to abhor good living and this is the best way to drive him out.

claims.statement: The patient will be the only one who knows that he is possessed.
claims.statement_id: Hanya si pasien yang tahu bahwa dirinya kerasukan (possessed).
claims.quote: The patient will be the only one who knows that he is possessed.

claims.statement: Sometimes the process appears to result in madness, and some patients run away into the bush.
claims.statement_id: Kadang proses itu tampaknya berujung pada kegilaan (madness), dan sebagian pasien melarikan diri ke semak belukar (bush).
claims.quote: Sometimes, however, the process appears to result in madness, and some patients run away into the bush.

claims.statement: In Central Africa the sufferer is supposed to be possessed by Mbwiri and can be relieved only by the intervention of the medicine-man or fetish.
claims.statement_id: Di Afrika Tengah, penderita dianggap dirasuki Mbwiri dan hanya dapat dipulihkan lewat campur tangan dukun (medicine-man) atau fetis.
claims.quote: In Central Africa the sufferer is supposed to be possessed by Mbwiri, and he can be relieved only by the intervention of the medicine-man or fetish.

claims.statement: A hut is built for him in the middle of the street, where he stays with the priest and his disciples until cured or maddened.
claims.statement_id: Di tengah jalan dibangun sebuah pondok (hut) untuknya, dan di sana ia tinggal bersama pendeta dan murid-muridnya sampai sembuh atau menjadi gila.
claims.quote: In the middle of the street a hut is built for his accommodation, and there he resides until cured, or maddened, along with the priest and his disciples.

claims.statement: There a continuous revel is held for ten days or a fortnight.
claims.statement_id: Di sana selama sepuluh hari atau dua minggu (ten days or a fortnight) diadakan pesta pora tanpa henti (continuous revel).
claims.quote: There for ten days or a fortnight a continuous revel is held

claims.statement: For obvious reasons the fetish-man gives out that Mbwiri regards good living with aversion.
claims.statement_id: Dengan alasan yang jelas, sang fetis (dukun) menyatakan bahwa Mbwiri tidak menyukai hidup enak (good living).
claims.quote: For obvious reasons the fetish gives out that Mbwiri regards good living with aversion.

claims.statement: The patient dances, usually shamming madness, until the epileptic attack comes on.
claims.statement_id: Pasien menari, biasanya berpura-pura gila, sampai serangan epilepsi (epileptic attack) datang.
claims.quote: The patient dances, usually shamming madness, until the epileptic attack comes on

claims.statement: After a cure he avoids certain kinds of food and performs certain duties; sometimes the process ends in the patient's insanity.
claims.statement_id: Setelah sembuh, ia menghindari jenis makanan tertentu dan menjalankan kewajiban tertentu; kadang proses itu berakhir dengan kegilaan (insanity) si pasien.
claims.quote: avoids certain kinds of food, and performs certain duties. Sometimes the process terminates in the patient's insanity

claims.statement: When such a possession occurs the shaman is called, and a hut is built where the afflicted stays with the shaman and his assistants until cured.
claims.statement_id: Bila kerasukan seperti itu terjadi, dukun (shaman) dipanggil; sebuah pondok (hut) dibangun tempat penderita tinggal bersama dukun dan para pembantunya sampai sembuh.
claims.quote: When such a possession occurs, the shaman is called. A hut is built in which the afflicted resides along with the shaman and his assistants until he is cured.

claims.statement: For ten days or a fortnight these people eat and drink at the expense of the patient's relatives and dance to flute and drum.
claims.statement_id: Selama sepuluh hari atau dua minggu, mereka makan dan minum atas biaya kerabat pasien (patient's relatives) serta menari diiringi seruling dan gendang (flute and drum).
claims.quote: For ten days or a fortnight, these people eat and drink at the expense of the patient's relatives and dance to the music of flute and drum.

claims.statement: Khanyapa is a mythical creature of the Basotho people of Southern Africa.
claims.statement_id: Khanyapa adalah makhluk mitos dari orang Basotho di Afrika bagian selatan (Southern Africa).
claims.quote: is a mythical creature from the Basotho people of Southern Africa.

claims.statement: It is described as a shapeless, gluttonous monster that swallows every living thing it meets and grows larger the more it swallows; it has multiple sharp tongues used as weapons.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai monster rakus tanpa bentuk (shapeless, gluttonous monster) yang menelan semua makhluk hidup yang dijumpainya dan makin besar setiap kali menelan; ia punya banyak lidah tajam yang dipakai sebagai senjata.
claims.quote: It is described as a shapeless, gluttonous monster that swallows everything living it comes by and gets larger and larger the more it swallows. It has multiple sharp tongues which it uses as weapons.

claims.statement: Khanyapa is the main antagonist of the story of Ditaolane, where the monster symbolizes all that holds back humanity and is killed by the hero.
claims.statement_id: Khanyapa adalah tokoh antagonis utama dalam kisah Ditaolane; di sana monster itu melambangkan segala hal yang menahan kemanusiaan (holds back humanity) dan dibunuh oleh sang pahlawan.
claims.quote: Khanyapa is the main antagonist in the story of Ditaolane where the monster is symbolic of all that holds back humanity and is killed by the hero.

claims.statement: Kgodumodumo is an archaic Sotho term most likely meaning "great noise".
claims.statement_id: Kgodumodumo adalah istilah Sotho kuno yang kemungkinan besar berarti "suara besar" (great noise).
claims.quote: Kgodumodumo is an archaic Sotho term, most likely meaning “great noise”.

claims.statement: Archeologists believe Khanyapa was influenced by the San people's python god.
claims.statement_id: Para arkeolog meyakini Khanyapa dipengaruhi oleh dewa piton (python god) orang San.
claims.quote: Archeologists believe Khanyapa is influenced by the San people’s python god.

claims.statement: It is also known as Kholumolumo in Lesotho Sesotho and Kgodumodumo in South African Sesotho.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini juga dikenal sebagai Kholumolumo dalam bahasa Sesotho Lesotho dan Kgodumodumo dalam bahasa Sesotho Afrika Selatan (South African Sesotho).
claims.quote: also known as Kholumolumo in Lesotho Sesotho and Kgodumodumo in South African Sesotho

claims.statement: An animal called Kammapa devoured them all, large and small; it was a horrible beast.
claims.statement_id: Seekor binatang luar biasa bernama Kammapa melahap semua manusia, besar dan kecil; ia binatang yang mengerikan (horrible beast).
claims.quote: called Kammapa, devoured them all, large and small. It was a horrible beast

claims.statement: Its body was so long that the sharpest eyes could hardly see it all at once.
claims.statement_id: Tubuhnya begitu panjang sehingga mata paling tajam pun hampir tak dapat melihat seluruhnya sekaligus (sharpest eyes could hardly see it all at once).
claims.quote: that the sharpest eyes could hardly see it all at once.

claims.statement: The child (Litaolane) had already reached the stature of a full-grown man and was uttering words full of wisdom.
claims.statement_id: Bayi itu (Litaolane) sudah mencapai tinggi orang dewasa (full-grown man) dan mengucapkan kata-kata penuh hikmat.
claims.quote: the child had already reached the stature of a full-grown man, and was uttering words full of wisdom.

claims.statement: He went to attack the devourer of the world; Kammapa opened his frightful jaws and swallowed him up.
claims.statement_id: Ia pergi menyerang sang pelahap dunia (devourer of the world); Kammapa membuka rahangnya yang mengerikan dan menelannya.
claims.quote: the devourer of the world. Kammapa opened his frightful jaws, and swallowed him up

claims.statement: Armed with his knife he entered the monster's stomach and tore its entrails; Kammapa gave a terrible roar and fell.
claims.statement_id: Bersenjatakan pisau (knife), ia masuk ke perut monster itu dan merobek isi perutnya; Kammapa meraung dahsyat lalu tumbang.
claims.quote: he entered, armed with his knife, into the stomach of the monster, and tore his entrails. Kammapa gave a terrible roar, and fell.

claims.statement: Casalis adds that the natives declare themselves unable to explain this extraordinary legend.
claims.statement_id: Casalis menambahkan bahwa penduduk setempat (natives) menyatakan diri tidak mampu menjelaskan legenda yang luar biasa ini.
claims.quote: I must add that the natives declare themselves incapable of giving the explanation of this extraordinary legend.

claims.statement: Long ago a huge, shapeless thing called Khodumodumo (some call it Kammapa) appeared and swallowed every living creature in its way.
claims.statement_id: Menurut orang Basuto, dahulu muncul sesuatu yang sangat besar tanpa bentuk bernama Khodumodumo (sebagian orang menyebutnya Kammapa) yang menelan setiap makhluk hidup di jalannya.
claims.quote: Once upon a time there appeared in our country a huge, shapeless thing called Khodumodumo (but some people call it Kammapa). It swallowed every living creature that came in its way.

claims.statement: On reaching the narrow pass (nek) at the valley entrance it had swelled so much that it could not get through and had to stay there.
claims.statement_id: Saat mencapai celah sempit (nek) di mulut lembah, tubuhnya sudah begitu membengkak sehingga tak bisa lewat dan terpaksa diam di situ.
claims.quote: when it reached the narrow pass (or nek) at the entrance to the valley it had swelled to such a size that it could not get through, and was forced to stay where it was.

claims.statement: A woman smeared herself all over with ashes and ran into the calves' pen.
claims.statement_id: Seorang perempuan melumuri seluruh tubuhnya dengan abu (ashes) lalu lari ke kandang anak sapi (calves' pen).
claims.quote: smeared herself all over with ashes, and ran into the calves’ pen

claims.statement: The Basuto tell the legend as follows.
claims.statement_id: Orang Basuto menuturkan legenda ini sebagai berikut.
claims.quote: The Basuto tell the legend as follows.

claims.statement: Usiququmadevu or Isiququmadevu is a creature of Zulu mythology, a bearded, bloated monster who eats every living thing she comes across.
claims.statement_id: Usiququmadevu atau Isiququmadevu adalah makhluk dari mitologi Zulu; ia monster betina berjanggut dan menggembung (bearded, bloated monster) yang memakan setiap makhluk hidup yang dijumpainya.
claims.quote: Usiququmadevu or Isiququmadevu is a creature from Zulu mythology. She is a bearded, bloated monster who eats every living thing she comes across.

claims.statement: Usiququmadevu is said to have a husband of the same name.
claims.statement_id: Usiququmadevu konon memiliki suami (husband) dengan nama yang sama.
claims.quote: Usiququmadevu is said to have a husband of the same name.

claims.statement: According to legend she came upon a chief's unguarded children and quickly swallowed them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, suatu hari ia menemukan anak-anak seorang kepala suku (chief) yang tidak dijaga dan segera menelan mereka.
claims.quote: According to legend, one day she came upon the children of a chief. As they were unguarded, she quickly swallowed them.

claims.statement: He soon found her and killed her by stabbing her in the hump; his children came out unscathed from her mouth.
claims.statement_id: Sang kepala suku segera menemukannya dan membunuhnya dengan menikam punuknya (hump); anak-anaknya keluar tanpa cedera dari mulutnya.
claims.quote: Soon he did and killed her by stabbing her in the hump; his children emerged unscathed from her mouth.

claims.statement: Usiququmadevu, also known as Isiququmadevu, is a creature of Zulu mythology: a bearded, bloated female monster (mostro barbuto e gonfio di sesso femminile) that eats every living creature in its path.
claims.statement_id: Usiququmadevu, juga dikenal sebagai Isiququmadevu, adalah makhluk mitologi Zulu: monster betina berjanggut dan menggembung (mostro barbuto e gonfio di sesso femminile) yang memakan setiap makhluk hidup di jalannya.
claims.quote: Usiququmadevu, conosciuta anche con il nome di Isiququmadevu, è una creatura appartenente alla mitologia Zulu. È un mostro barbuto e gonfio di sesso femminile, che mangia ogni creatura vivente che trova nel suo cammino.

claims.statement: The monster lives in the Ilulange, a mythical river that cannot be located today; the names used for it in the story show it is regarded as female.
claims.statement_id: Monster ini tinggal di Ilulange, sungai mitis (mythical river) yang kini tak dapat ditemukan lokasinya; nama-nama yang dipakai dalam kisah menunjukkan bahwa ia dianggap betina (female).
claims.quote: lives in the Ilulange, a mythical river not to be located nowadays. The names applied to this monster in the course of the story show that it is looked upon as a female.

claims.statement: Callaway explains the word as meaning a bloated, squatting, bearded monster.
claims.statement_id: Callaway menjelaskan kata ini berarti monster yang menggembung, berjongkok, dan berjanggut (bloated, squatting, bearded monster).
claims.quote: Callaway explains this word to mean ... a bloated, squatting, bearded monster

claims.statement: The creature appears in the Zulu tale of Untombinde.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini muncul dalam kisah Zulu tentang Untombinde (tale of Untombinde).
claims.quote: In the Zulu tale of Untombinde the isiququmadevu

claims.statement: Untombinde, who refused to petition the monster, was immediately seized and dragged down into the water.
claims.statement_id: Untombinde, yang menolak memohon kepada monster itu, langsung ditangkap dan diseret ke dalam air (water).
claims.quote: and was immediately seized by the monster and dragged down into the water.

claims.statement: The warriors found the monster squatting on the river-bank and were all swallowed before they could attack her.
claims.statement_id: Para prajurit (warriors) yang dikirim menemukan monster itu berjongkok di tepi sungai dan semuanya ditelan sebelum sempat menyerang.
claims.quote: The warriors found the monster squatting on the river-bank, and were swallowed up, every one, before they could attack her.

claims.statement: She then swallowed all the inhabitants of the chief's kraal with their dogs and cattle, and all the people of the surrounding country.
claims.statement_id: Ia lalu menelan seluruh penghuni kraal kepala suku beserta anjing dan ternak mereka (dogs and cattle), juga semua orang di sekitarnya.
claims.quote: swallowed up all the inhabitants, with their dogs and their cattle, as well as all the people in the surrounding country.

claims.statement: The father came and stabbed the lump, and so the monster died.
claims.statement_id: Sang ayah datang dan menikam benjolan (lump) itu, dan monster itu pun mati.
claims.quote: came and stabbed the lump, and so the hiququmadevu died.

claims.statement: Werner notes that the father as deliverer is an important variation.
claims.statement_id: Werner mencatat bahwa sang ayah sebagai penyelamat (father as deliverer) merupakan variasi penting.
claims.quote: The father as deliverer is an important variation.

claims.statement: An obayifo is a vampire/witch-like mythological creature from West Africa, from the folklore of the Ashanti.
claims.statement_id: Obayifo adalah makhluk mitologis mirip vampir/penyihir (vampire/witch-like) dari Afrika Barat yang berasal dari cerita rakyat Ashanti.
claims.quote: An obayifo is a vampire/witch-like mythological creature from West Africa coming from the folklore of the Ashanti.

claims.statement: In Ashanti folklore obayifo are very common and may inhabit the bodies of any man or woman; they are described as having shifty eyes and being obsessed with food.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Ashanti, obayifo sangat umum dan dapat menghuni tubuh laki-laki atau perempuan mana pun; mereka digambarkan bermata jelalatan (shifty eyes) dan terobsesi pada makanan.
claims.quote: In Ashanti folklore, obayifo are very common and may inhabit the bodies of any man or woman. They are described as having shifty eyes and being obsessed with food.

claims.statement: When travelling at night they are said to emit a phosphorescent light from their armpits and anus.
claims.statement_id: Saat bepergian pada malam hari, mereka konon memancarkan cahaya fosforesen (phosphorescent light) dari ketiak dan anus.
claims.quote: When travelling at night they are said to emit a phosphorescent light from their armpits and anus.

claims.statement: The obayifo is regarded as similar to the asiman of the Dahomey people, a creature that can shapeshift and fly, turning into a ball of light and hunting prey in the night sky.
claims.statement_id: Obayifo dianggap serupa dengan asiman pada orang Dahomey, makhluk yang dapat berubah wujud dan terbang, menjadi bola cahaya, dan berburu mangsa di langit malam.
claims.quote: The obayifo is known as a similar entity to the asiman by the Dahomey people, a creature that can shapeshift and fly, turning itself into a ball of light and hunting for prey in the night sky.

claims.statement: In Ashanti Twi the word for witchcraft is bayi, though the etymology of bayi is still uncertain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Twi Ashanti, kata untuk ilmu sihir (witchcraft) adalah bayi; meski begitu, etimologi bayi masih belum pasti.
claims.quote: In Ashanti Twi, the word used to describe witchcraft is bayi. Despite this, the etymology of bayi is still uncertain.

claims.statement: Another possible reading is oba meaning "child" and yi meaning to remove.
claims.statement_id: Kemungkinan lain adalah oba yang berarti "anak" (child) dan yi yang berarti mengambil atau menyingkirkan (to remove).
claims.quote: Another possible variation is oba meaning "child" and yi meaning to remove.

claims.statement: People, typically women, who practiced bayi turned into the obayifo.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang mempraktikkan bayi, biasanya perempuan (typically women), berubah menjadi obayifo.
claims.quote: People, typically women, who practiced bayi turned into the obayifo.

claims.statement: Obansam, meaning wizard, was used exclusively for males, while obayifo was sometimes used exclusively for women.
claims.statement_id: Obansam, yang berarti penyihir laki-laki (wizard), dipakai khusus untuk laki-laki, sedangkan obayifo kadang dipakai khusus untuk perempuan.
claims.quote: obansam, meaning wizard, was a term used for the males exclusively as obayifo was sometimes only used for women exclusively.

claims.statement: Obayifo describes both men and women who practiced bayi and turned into the monster.
claims.statement_id: Istilah obayifo dipakai untuk laki-laki maupun perempuan yang mempraktikkan bayi dan berubah menjadi monster (turned into the monster).
claims.quote: Although obayifo is used to describe both the men and women who practiced bayi and turned into the monster

claims.statement: Obayifo is a vampire-like (podobná upírovi) mythological being from West Africa (Západní Afriky), from the folklore of the Ashanti (Ašanti).
claims.statement_id: Obayifo adalah makhluk mitologis mirip vampir (podobná upírovi) dari Afrika Barat (Západní Afriky) yang berasal dari folklor suku Ashanti (Ašanti).
claims.quote: Obayifo je mytologická bytost podobná upírovi ze Západní Afriky, která pochází z místního folklóru kmene Ašanti.

claims.statement: Obayifo was also regarded as a kind of witch (čarodějnice).
claims.statement_id: Obayifo juga dianggap sejenis penyihir perempuan (čarodějnice).
claims.quote: Obayifo byl považován také za druh čarodějnice.

claims.statement: When travelling at night (v noci) they are said to give off a phosphorescent light (fosforeskující světlo) from their armpits and anus.
claims.statement_id: Saat bepergian pada malam hari (v noci), mereka konon memancarkan cahaya fosforesen (fosforeskující světlo) dari ketiak dan dubur.
claims.quote: Při cestování v noci mají vydávat fosforeskující světlo vycházející z jejich podpaží a řitního otvoru.

claims.statement: The reading "to remove a child" here highlights a close association of infant mortality and fertility with witchcraft.
claims.statement_id: Tafsiran "menyingkirkan anak" dalam hal ini menyoroti kaitan erat antara kematian bayi (infant mortality), kesuburan, dan ilmu sihir.
claims.quote: in this case highlights a close association of infant mortality and fertility to the likes of witchcraft.

claims.statement: Ọgbanje is a term in Odinani for what was thought to be an evil spirit that would deliberately plague a family with misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Ọgbanje adalah istilah dalam Odinani untuk apa yang dahulu dianggap roh jahat (evil spirit) yang sengaja menimpakan kemalangan pada sebuah keluarga.
claims.quote: is a term in Odinani ... for what was thought to be an evil spirit that would deliberately plague a family with misfortune.

claims.statement: Belief in ọgbanje in Igboland is not as strong as it once was, although there are still some believers.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada ọgbanje di tanah Igbo (Igboland) tidak sekuat dahulu, walaupun masih ada yang memercayainya.
claims.quote: Belief in ọgbanje in Igboland is not as strong as it once was, although there are still some believers.

claims.statement: Its literal meaning in the Igbo language is "children who come and go".
claims.statement_id: Arti harfiahnya dalam bahasa Igbo adalah "anak-anak yang datang dan pergi" (children who come and go).
claims.quote: Its literal meaning in the Igbo language is "children who come and go".

claims.statement: The word ọgbanje is often translated as changeling because of its similarity to the fairy changelings of Celtic and broader European mythology.
claims.statement_id: Kata ọgbanje sering diterjemahkan sebagai changeling karena kemiripannya dengan changeling peri dalam mitologi Kelt (Celtic) dan Eropa (European) pada umumnya.
claims.quote: The word ọgbanje is often translated as changeling, due to the similarities they share with the fairy changelings of Celtic and broader European mythology.

claims.statement: Some theorists hypothesize that these ideas were mythological ways of understanding once-unknown diseases that often killed children (such as SIDS and sickle cell disease).
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah teoretikus menduga konsep ini menjadi cara mitologis untuk memahami penyakit yang dahulu belum dikenal dan sering merenggut nyawa anak-anak (seperti SIDS dan penyakit sel sabit, sickle cell disease).
claims.quote: Some theorists have hypothesized that these conceptions serve as mythological ways of understanding what were once unknown diseases that often claimed the lives of children (such as SIDS and sickle cell disease)

claims.statement: The ọgbanje was believed to deliberately die and be reborn into the family's next child, repeating the cycle and causing much grief.
claims.statement_id: Ọgbanje dipercaya sengaja mati lalu lahir kembali sebagai anak berikutnya dalam keluarga itu dan mengulang siklusnya, menimbulkan banyak duka (grief).
claims.quote: the ọgbanje would deliberately die and then be reborn into the next child of the family and repeat the cycle, causing much grief.

claims.statement: The evil spirits are said to have stones called iyi-uwa, which they bury somewhere secret.
claims.statement_id: Roh-roh jahat ini konon memiliki batu yang disebut iyi-uwa (stones called iyi-uwa) yang mereka kubur di tempat rahasia.
claims.quote: The evil spirits are said to have stones called iyi-uwa, which they bury somewhere secret.

claims.statement: Finding the evil spirits' iyi-uwa ensures the ọgbanje will never again plague the family with misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Menemukan iyi-uwa roh jahat itu menjamin ọgbanje tidak lagi menimpakan kemalangan (misfortune) pada keluarga tersebut.
claims.quote: Finding the evil spirits' iyi-uwa ensures the ọgbanje would never again plague the family with misfortune.

claims.statement: The iyi-uwa is dug out by a priest and destroyed.
claims.statement_id: Iyi-uwa digali oleh seorang pendeta (priest) lalu dihancurkan.
claims.quote: The iyi-uwa is dug out by a priest and destroyed.

claims.statement: To keep the ọgbanje from returning after the child's death, the body would be cut or mutilated; yet some ọgbanje were said to return bearing the scars.
claims.statement_id: Untuk mencegah ọgbanje kembali setelah anak itu meninggal, jasadnya dilukai atau dimutilasi (cut or mutilated); namun ada ọgbanje yang konon kembali dengan membawa bekas luka mutilasi itu (scars).
claims.quote: To prevent the ọgbanje from returning after the child's death, they would be cut or mutilated. Some ọgbanje, however, were said to return bearing the physical scars of the mutilation.

claims.statement: Other signs that helped families identify them were birthmarks, a child's first words, and behavior resembling the child who had been reincarnated.
claims.statement_id: Tanda lain yang membantu keluarga mengenalinya adalah tanda lahir (birthmarks), kata-kata pertama, dan kemiripan perilaku dengan anak yang bereinkarnasi.
claims.quote: Other things that have helped families identify them are birthmarks the child had, the first words they said, and behavior similarities from the child that has been reincarnated.

claims.statement: In Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart (1958), the character Ezinma was considered an ọgbanje.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Chinua Achebe, Things Fall Apart (1958), tokoh Ezinma dianggap seorang ọgbanje.
claims.quote: In the critically acclaimed novel by Chinua Achebe, Things Fall Apart (1958), the character Ezinma was considered an ọgbanje

claims.statement: In the novel Freshwater by Akwaeke Emezi (2018), the main character Ada is an ọgbanje.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Freshwater karya Akwaeke Emezi (2018), tokoh utamanya, Ada, adalah seorang ọgbanje.
claims.quote: In the novel Freshwater by Akwaeke Emezi (2018), the main character, Ada, is an ọgbanje

claims.statement: Ben Okri's Booker Prize-winning novel The Famished Road (1991) also features the figure.
claims.statement_id: Novel Ben Okri pemenang Booker Prize, The Famished Road (1991), juga memuat sosok ini.
claims.quote: In Ben Okri's Booker Prize-winning novel, The Famished Road (1991)

claims.statement: The character Azaro is a spirit child, or ogbanje, who travels between worlds.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh Azaro adalah anak roh (spirit child) atau ogbanje yang berkelana di antara dunia-dunia.
claims.quote: the character Azaro is a spirit child, or ogbanje, who travels between worlds.

claims.statement: Its plain translation in the Igbo language (asụsụ Igbo) is "children who come and go" (ụmụaka ndị na-abịa ma na-aga).
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan harfiahnya dalam bahasa Igbo (asụsụ Igbo) adalah "anak-anak yang datang dan pergi" (ụmụaka ndị na-abịa ma na-aga).
claims.quote: Nsụgharị nkịtị ya n'asụsụ Igbo bụ "ụmụaka ndị na-abịa ma na-aga".

claims.statement: Belief in Ọgbanje in the Igbo land (ala Igbo) is not as strong as before (adịghị ike dịka ọ dịrị na mbụ), though some still believe in it.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada Ọgbanje di tanah Igbo (ala Igbo) tidak sekuat dahulu (adịghị ike dịka ọ dịrị na mbụ), walau masih ada yang memercayainya.
claims.quote: Nkwenye n' Ọgbanje n'ala Igbo adịghị ike dịka ọ dịrị na mbụ ọ bụ ezie na-enwekwara ụfọdụ ndị kwere na ya.

claims.statement: Sickle cell disease (Ọrịa Sickle cell) may have contributed to this belief (nkwenkwe a).
claims.statement_id: Penyakit sel sabit (Ọrịa Sickle cell) mungkin turut menyumbang pada kepercayaan ini (nkwenkwe a).
claims.quote: Ọrịa Sickle cell nwere ike inye aka na nkwenkwe a

claims.statement: In the mythology of the Oromo people of Ethiopia, Holawaka is a legendary bird sent by the gods as a messenger to humanity.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi orang Oromo di Etiopia (Ethiopia), Holawaka adalah burung legendaris yang diutus para dewa sebagai pembawa pesan bagi umat manusia.
claims.quote: In the mythology of the Oromo people of Ethiopia, Holawaka is a legendary bird sent by the gods as a messenger to humanity.

claims.statement: The gods told Holawaka to tell humans they would be immortal and need only strip off their skins to be rejuvenated.
claims.statement_id: Para dewa memerintahkan Holawaka memberi tahu manusia bahwa mereka akan abadi (immortal) dan cukup melepaskan kulit (strip off their skins) untuk menjadi muda kembali.
claims.quote: The gods instructed Holawaka to tell humans that they would be immortal and all that they needed to do to be rejuvenated was to strip off their skins.

claims.statement: On its way to deliver the message, however, Holawaka met a snake eating an animal carcass.
claims.statement_id: Namun dalam perjalanan menyampaikan pesan itu, Holawaka bertemu seekor ular (snake) yang sedang memakan bangkai hewan.
claims.quote: However, on its way to deliver the message, Holawaka encountered a snake eating an animal carcass.

claims.statement: The bird begged the snake to share the food, and the snake agreed only when Holawaka offered to share the message it carried.
claims.statement_id: Burung itu memohon agar ular berbagi makanan, tetapi ular baru setuju setelah Holawaka menawarkan untuk membagi pesan (message) yang dibawanya.
claims.quote: The bird pleaded with the snake to share some of the food, but the snake only agreed when Holawaka offered to share the message it was carrying.

claims.statement: It told the snake that humans will die when they grow old, but snakes need only shed their skin to become young again.
claims.statement_id: Holawaka berkata kepada ular bahwa manusia akan mati bila menua, sedangkan ular cukup berganti kulit (shed their skin) untuk muda kembali.
claims.quote: It told the snake that when humans grow old they will die, but when snakes grow old all they have to do is shed their skin to become young again.

claims.statement: As punishment for dooming mankind to mortality, the gods inflicted a terrible disease on Holawaka, so that it cries out in pain forever.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai hukuman karena membuat manusia fana (mortal), para dewa menimpakan penyakit mengerikan (terrible disease) pada Holawaka sehingga ia menjerit kesakitan selamanya.
claims.quote: As punishment for dooming mankind to a mortal existence, the gods inflicted a terrible disease upon Holawaka, causing it to cry out in pain forever.

claims.statement: Holawaka, in the mythology of the galla of Ethiopia (Etiopia), is a legendary messenger bird (leggendario uccello messaggero).
claims.statement_id: Holawaka, dalam mitologi orang galla di Etiopia (Etiopia), adalah burung pembawa pesan yang legendaris (leggendario uccello messaggero).
claims.quote: Holawaka, nella mitologia dei galla dell'Etiopia, è un leggendario uccello messaggero.

claims.statement: During the journey, out of hunger (per fame), it revealed the secret to a snake (serpente), which gave it food in return.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perjalanan, karena lapar (per fame), ia membocorkan rahasia itu kepada seekor ular (serpente) yang sebagai gantinya memberinya makan.
claims.quote: Durante il viaggio per fame rivelò il segreto ad un serpente che in cambio gli diede da mangiare.

claims.statement: For this misdeed the gods (divinità) inflicted a terrible disease (terribile malattia) on the bird, so that its cries of pain are still heard today.
claims.statement_id: Karena kesalahan ini para dewa (divinità) menimpakan penyakit mengerikan (terribile malattia) pada burung itu, sehingga jeritan kesakitannya masih terdengar hingga kini.
claims.quote: Per questo misfatto le divinità inflissero al volatile una terribile malattia, per cui ancora oggi si odono e sue grida di dolore.

issues.message: Tidak muncul di kutipan mana pun: Africa. Tambahkan klaim yang kutipannya memuat hal ini, atau hapus dari teks.

claims.statement: Ilomba is a sea snake with destructive powers in the mythology of the Lozi people of Zambia.
claims.statement_id: Ilomba adalah ular laut (sea snake) berkekuatan merusak dalam mitologi orang Lozi di Zambia.
claims.quote: Ilomba is a sea snake with destructive powers in the mythology of the Lozi people of Zambia.

claims.statement: It is made from the maker's finger nails and blood from the forehead, back and chest.
claims.statement_id: Ia dibuat dari kuku jari (finger nails) dan darah dari dahi, punggung, dan dada pembuatnya.
claims.quote: It is made with their finger nails and blood from their forehead, back, and chest.

claims.statement: When young it is usually fed eggs and porridge because its fangs are not fully developed.
claims.statement_id: Saat masih muda ia biasanya diberi makan telur dan bubur (eggs and porridge) karena taringnya belum tumbuh sempurna.
claims.quote: It is usually fed with eggs and porridge when it is young because its fangs are not fully developed.

claims.statement: It takes on the identity of its owner, and the owner commands it to kill a person.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengambil identitas orang yang memilikinya (owner), dan pemiliknya akan memerintahkannya membunuh seseorang.
claims.quote: It takes on the identity of the person that owns it. The owner will command it to kill a person.

claims.statement: The victim sees the witch doctor's face in place of the Ilomba's, while others see a normal snake; it bites its prey and then consumes its soul.
claims.statement_id: Korbannya melihat wajah dukun (witch doctor) sebagai wajah Ilomba, sedangkan orang lain melihatnya sebagai ular biasa; ia menggigit mangsanya lalu memakan jiwanya (soul).
claims.quote: The victim will see the witch doctor's face in place of the Ilomba's, but the other people will view it as a normal snake. It bites into its prey then consumes its soul.

claims.statement: If it is killed, the owner feels the pain and then dies; if the owner dies, it dies.
claims.statement_id: Jika Ilomba dibunuh, pemiliknya merasakan sakit lalu mati; jika pemiliknya mati, Ilomba pun mati.
claims.quote: If it is killed, the owner feels the pain, and then dies. If the owner dies, it dies.

claims.statement: If the witch doctor stops feeding it, it will turn on its master and consume him.
claims.statement_id: Jika dukun berhenti memberinya makan, ia akan berbalik menyerang tuannya (master) dan memangsanya.
claims.quote: If the witch doctor stops supplying food to it, it will turn on its master and consume them.

claims.statement: The ilomba is a water-snake familiar created by a sorcerer either for himself or for a client.
claims.statement_id: Ilomba adalah familiar berwujud ular air (water-snake familiar) yang dibuat oleh tukang sihir (sorcerer) untuk dirinya sendiri atau untuk kliennya.
claims.quote: The ilomba is a water-snake familiar which is created by a sorcerer either for himself or for a client.

claims.statement: Its body is a snake's, but its head is human in form and closely resembles its owner's head.
claims.statement_id: Tubuhnya berupa ular, tetapi kepalanya berbentuk manusia dan sangat mirip kepala pemiliknya (head of its owner).
claims.quote: The body of the creature is that of a snake, but the head is human in form and closely resembles the head of its owner.

claims.statement: The ilomba is so closely linked to its owner that its destruction must result in the owner's death.
claims.statement_id: Ilomba begitu erat terikat dengan pemiliknya sehingga kehancurannya pasti menyebabkan kematian sang pemilik (death of the latter).
claims.quote: so closely linked to their owners that their destruction must result in the death of the latter.

claims.statement: It is also known as lilombamema or, among the Kaonde, mulombe.
claims.statement_id: Ilomba juga dikenal sebagai lilombamema, atau mulombe oleh orang Kaonde.
claims.quote: otherwise known as lilombamema or, by the Kaonde, mulombe

claims.statement: Reynolds calls it the best known of all central African familiars and the only one with much literature.
claims.statement_id: Reynolds menyebut ilomba sebagai familiar paling terkenal di Afrika tengah (central African familiars) dan satu-satunya yang banyak dibahas dalam literatur.
claims.quote: The best known of all central African familiars, and the only one on which there is much literature

claims.statement: Soon it demands meat: a foetus, then a babe and finally an adult.
claims.statement_id: Tak lama kemudian ia menuntut daging (meat): janin, lalu bayi, dan akhirnya orang dewasa.
claims.quote: Soon it demands meat—a foetus, then a babe and finally an adult.

claims.statement: In one account the snake chose to live in the river, and its owner found that it could talk.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kesaksian, ular itu memilih tinggal di sungai (river) dan pemiliknya mendapati bahwa ia bisa berbicara.
claims.quote: The snake chose to live in the river, and he found that it could talk.

claims.statement: Another fate for the ilomba's owner is its discovery by a witchdoctor, who shoots it with a wuta wawufuku.
claims.statement_id: Nasib lain bagi pemilik ilomba adalah bila ilomba ditemukan oleh dukun (witchdoctor) yang menembaknya dengan senapan wuta wawufuku.
claims.quote: An alternative fate for the owner of the ilomba is its discovery by a witchdoctor who then shoots it with a wuta wawufuku

claims.statement: In chiKaranga folklore (munhema/ruambanhema), the Deverangwena is said to be a kind of beast (chikara) resembling a fish (chinenge hove).
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat (munhema/ruambanhema) chiKaranga, Deverangwena disebut sejenis binatang (chikara) yang menyerupai ikan (chinenge hove).
claims.quote: Deverangwena munhema (kana ruambanhema) dze chiKaranga inonzi imhando ye chikara cheruandhle chinenge hove,

claims.statement: It is said to follow (chinotevera) the crocodile (ngwena or garwe) in the water (mumvuura).
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu dikatakan mengikuti (chinotevera) buaya (ngwena atau garwe) di dalam air (mumvuura).
claims.quote: chainzi chinotevera ngwena (kana garwe) mumvuura.

claims.statement: Because of that habit (tsika), people (vanhu) called it deverangwena.
claims.statement_id: Karena kebiasaan (tsika) itulah orang-orang (vanhu) menyebutnya deverangwena.
claims.quote: Nekuda kwe tsika yayo iyoyo, zvakakonzera kuti vanhu vaidane kuti deverangwena.

claims.statement: Moreover, it has no equivalent name in English (paChingezi).
claims.statement_id: Selain itu, tidak ada padanan namanya dalam bahasa Inggris (paChingezi).
claims.quote: uyezve hapana fanadudziro rayo paChingezi.

claims.statement: Garwe or ngwena (crocodile in English) is an animal that lives in water (mumvura).
claims.statement_id: Garwe atau ngwena (crocodile dalam bahasa Inggris) adalah hewan yang hidup di air (mumvura).
claims.quote: Garwe, ngwena, gambinga, gomombo (crocodile in English) imhuka inogara mumvura

claims.statement: The Bemba, Fwe, Zigula and Yao also say ngwena (crocodile) for garwe.
claims.statement_id: Orang Bemba, Fwe, Zigula, dan Yao juga menyebut buaya (crocodile) ngwena.
claims.quote: VaBemba, VaFwe, VaZigula neVaYao vanoti ngwena (crocodile) kureva garwe.

claims.statement: The Hira is a mythical monster in epic and folk tales of the Songhai people, especially the Bozo, who traditionally lived by hunting and fishing along the Niger River.
claims.statement_id: Hira adalah monster mitos dalam kisah epik dan cerita rakyat orang Songhai, khususnya orang Bozo yang secara tradisional hidup dari berburu dan menangkap ikan di sepanjang Sungai Niger.
claims.quote: The Hira is a mythical monster who occurs in epic and folklore tales of the Songhai people, particularly the Bozo people who traditionally lived from hunting and fishing along the Niger River.

claims.statement: The main source is the tales collected by M. A. Dupuis Yakouba at the start of the twentieth century.
claims.statement_id: Sumber utamanya adalah kisah-kisah yang dikumpulkan M. A. Dupuis Yakouba pada awal abad ke-20 (twentieth century).
claims.quote: The main source are the tales collected by M. A. Dupuis Yakouba at the start of the twentieth century.

claims.statement: The Hira is a legendary kind of buffalo known for incredible force and brutality.
claims.statement_id: Hira adalah sejenis kerbau (buffalo) legendaris yang terkenal karena kekuatan luar biasa dan kebrutalannya.
claims.quote: The Hira is a legendary variety of buffalo known for incredible force and brutality.

claims.statement: The Hira is the main opponent in one of the epic tales about the culture hero Moussa Gname.
claims.statement_id: Hira adalah lawan utama (main opponent) dalam salah satu kisah epik tentang pahlawan budaya Moussa Gname.
claims.quote: The Hira is the main opponent in one of the epic tales about the culture hero Moussa Gname

claims.statement: A second Hira comes, and a diviner says it can only be killed by a female elephant disguised as the chief's girlfriend.
claims.statement_id: Hira kedua datang, dan seorang peramal (diviner) berkata monster itu hanya bisa dibunuh oleh seekor gajah betina (female elephant) yang menyamar sebagai kekasih sang kepala.
claims.quote: A second Hira comes, and a diviner says that the monster can only be killed by a female elephant--who is disguised as the chief's girlfriend.

claims.statement: She pulls four hairs from its tail and gives them to Moussa; next day Moussa only has to show the Hira its own hairs for it to lie down and be killed.
claims.statement_id: Gajah betina itu mencabut empat helai bulu ekor Hira (four hairs from his tail) dan memberikannya kepada Moussa; esoknya Moussa cukup menunjukkan bulu itu agar monster itu berbaring dan dibunuh.
claims.quote: She pulls four hairs from his tail and gives them to Moussa; the next day, all Moussa has to do is show the Hira his own hairs for the monster to lie down and be killed.

claims.statement: The Hira is a buffalo (buffle) famed for its strength (force) and brutality.
claims.statement_id: Hira adalah kerbau (buffle) yang terkenal karena kekuatan (force) dan kebrutalannya.
claims.quote: Hira, buffle réputé pour sa force et sa brutalité.

claims.statement: It was a wicked beast (bête méchante) that terrorised the whole bush (brousse).
claims.statement_id: Hira adalah binatang jahat (bête méchante) yang meneror seluruh semak belantara (brousse).
claims.quote: C'était une bête méchante qui terrorisait toute la brousse.

claims.statement: No hunter (chasseur) went hunting any more, and nobody dared venture into the bush.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada pemburu (chasseur) yang berani berburu, dan tak seorang pun berani masuk ke semak belantara.
claims.quote: Aucun chasseur n'allait plus à la chasse : personne n'osait s'aventurer dans la brousse.

claims.statement: Kourouyoré struck the Hira with his spear (lance) and it broke; his arrows (flèches) broke too.
claims.statement_id: Kourouyoré menusuk Hira dengan tombak (lance) dan tombak itu patah; panah-panahnya (flèches) pun patah.
claims.quote: Il le frappa de sa lance, elle se brisa ; il lui jeta des flèches, elles se brisèrent;

claims.statement: The Hira seized Kourouyoré, lifted him and threw him to the ground (jeta à terre).
claims.statement_id: Hira mengangkat Kourouyoré dan membantingnya ke tanah (jeta à terre).
claims.quote: Le Hira le prit, le souleva et le jeta à terre;

claims.statement: Mousa drew his knife (couteau) and cut the Hira's throat.
claims.statement_id: Mousa mencabut pisaunya (couteau) dan menggorok Hira.
claims.quote: Mousa tira son couteau et égorgea le Hira.

claims.statement: The Hira rose and changed into an elephant (se transforma en éléphant), and Meynsata fought it.
claims.statement_id: Hira bangkit lagi dan berubah wujud menjadi gajah (se transforma en éléphant), lalu Meynsata melawannya.
claims.quote: Il se leva et se transforma en éléphant; Meynsata lui rom-

claims.statement: Mousa struck the elephant and turned it into a lion (lion), then broke its neck.
claims.statement_id: Mousa memukul gajah itu dan mengubahnya menjadi singa (lion), lalu mematahkan lehernya.
claims.quote: Mousa aussi frappa l'éléphant et le transforma en lion, il lui rompit aussi le cou.

claims.statement: An elephant (éléphant), Sanou-Mandigné's friend, gave him the four hairs (quatre poils) and went back to the bush.
claims.statement_id: Seekor gajah (éléphant), sahabat Sanou-Mandigné, memberinya empat helai bulu (quatre poils) lalu kembali ke semak belantara.
claims.quote: l'éléphant lui donna les quatre poils et retourna dans la brousse.

claims.statement: Facing the Hira, Mousa showed it the four hairs of its tail (quatre poils de sa queue) and threw them at it.
