claims.statement_id: Ketika berhadapan dengan Hira, Mousa menunjukkan empat helai bulu ekornya (quatre poils de sa queue) dan melemparkannya kepadanya.
claims.quote: Quand il fut en présence du Hira, Mousa lui montra les quatre poils de sa queue et les lui jeta.

claims.statement: The Hira lay down (se coucha), and the Gow came up and cut its throat.
claims.statement_id: Hira pun berbaring (se coucha), lalu para Gow mendekat dan menggoroknya.

claims.statement: Jobar is a monster from the folklore of the Tuareg of Niger.
claims.statement_id: Jobar adalah monster dari cerita rakyat orang Tuareg di Niger.
claims.quote: Jobar is a monster from folklore of the Tuareg of Niger.

claims.statement: It was described as a giant camel-like beast and served as a boogeyman that would eat naughty children.
claims.statement_id: Jobar digambarkan sebagai binatang raksasa mirip unta (camel) dan berperan sebagai momok (boogeyman) yang memakan anak nakal.
claims.quote: It was described as a giant beast like a camel, and was as a boogeyman that would eat naughty children.

claims.statement: The dinosaur Jobaria was named after Jobar.
claims.statement_id: Dinosaurus Jobaria dinamai menurut Jobar.
claims.quote: The dinosaur Jobaria was named after Jobar

claims.statement: Bones of Jobaria eroding out of rocks were identified as belonging to Jobar.
claims.statement_id: Tulang-tulang Jobaria yang tersingkap dari batuan dianggap (identified) sebagai tulang Jobar.
claims.quote: as the bones of Jobaria eroding out of rocks were identified as belonging to Jobar.

claims.statement: Because the rocks showed a flood, there is a story of Jobars dying in a flood and a palaeontological theory that Jobaria died in one.
claims.statement_id: Karena batuan itu menunjukkan bekas banjir, ada kisah Jobar mati dalam banjir (flood) dan teori paleontologi bahwa Jobaria mati dalam banjir.
claims.quote: hence why there is a story of Jobars dying in a flood and a palaeontological theory Jobaria died in a flood.

claims.statement: The name of this dinosaur found in Niger comes from a mythical African creature called a Jobar, which was like a bogeyman.
claims.statement_id: Nama dinosaurus yang ditemukan di Niger ini berasal dari makhluk mitos Afrika (African) bernama Jobar yang mirip momok (bogeyman).
claims.quote: The imaginative name given to this monster found In Niger comes from a mythical African creature called a Jobar, who was like a bogeyman.

claims.statement: Tuareg children may be told: if you are not good (sage), the Jobar will come for you tonight (cette nuit).
claims.statement_id: Anak-anak Tuareg kadang diberi tahu: kalau kamu tidak baik (sage), Jobar akan datang menjemputmu malam ini (cette nuit).
claims.quote: Si tu n’es pas sage, le Jobar viendra te chercher cette nuit

claims.statement: The Jobar is a giant monster (monstre géant) belonging to Tuareg (touarègue) mythology.
claims.statement_id: Jobar adalah monster raksasa (monstre géant) yang menjadi bagian dari mitologi Tuareg (touarègue).
claims.quote: Monstre géant, le Jobar fait partie de la mythologie touarègue

claims.statement: It is also the name archaeologists gave a very large dinosaur (très grand dinosaure) whose skeleton was found in 1990 in the Agadez region.
claims.statement_id: Jobar juga menjadi nama yang diberikan para arkeolog kepada dinosaurus sangat besar (très grand dinosaure) yang kerangkanya ditemukan pada 1990 di wilayah Agadez.
claims.quote: c’est aussi le nom que des archéologues ont donné à un très grand dinosaure, dont le squelette a été retrouvé en 1990 dans la région d’Agadez.

claims.statement: The Koolakamba or Kooloo-Kamba is a purported hybrid species of chimpanzees and gorillas.
claims.statement_id: Koolakamba atau Kooloo-Kamba adalah spesies yang diduga hibrida (hybrid) simpanse dan gorila.
claims.quote: The Koolakamba or Kooloo-Kamba is a purported hybrid species of chimpanzees and gorillas.

claims.statement: This alleged hybrid ape has been reported in Africa since the mid 19th century, but no empirical evidence supports its existence.
claims.statement_id: Kera hibrida yang diduga ini dilaporkan di Afrika sejak pertengahan abad ke-19, tetapi tidak ada bukti empiris (empirical evidence) yang menguatkan keberadaannya.
claims.quote: This alleged hybrid ape species has been reported in Africa as early as the mid 19th century. No empirical evidence has been found to substantiate the existence of the creature.

claims.statement: Du Chaillu named the ape Koolakamba from words used by the indigenous Nkomi and Bakalai peoples in the Ovenga River region of West Central Africa, modern Gabon.
claims.statement_id: Du Chaillu menamai kera ini Koolakamba berdasarkan kata-kata penduduk asli (Nkomi dan Bakalai) di wilayah Sungai Ovenga, Afrika Barat Tengah, kini Gabon.
claims.quote: Du Chaillu refers to the ape as Koolakamba based upon his description of words used by the indigenous peoples (Nkomi and Bakalai) in the region of the Ovenga River of West Central Africa, modernly Gabon.

claims.statement: The Goumbi people called it kooloo-kamba from its noise or call, together with the Camma word kamba, which means to speak.
claims.statement_id: Orang Goumbi menyebutnya kooloo-kamba dari bunyi atau panggilannya (noise or call), ditambah kata Camma kamba yang berarti berbicara.
claims.quote: It was called kooloo-kamba by the Goumbi people, from its noise or call, ... and the Camma word kamba, which means

claims.statement: The Bakalai call it simply Koola.
claims.statement_id: Orang Bakalai menyebutnya cukup dengan Koola.
claims.quote: The Bakalai call it simply Koola.

claims.statement: The Koolakamba is supposed to be larger (plus grand), flatter-faced and more bipedal than the chimpanzee (chimpanzé).
claims.statement_id: Koolakamba dianggap lebih besar (plus grand), berwajah lebih datar, dan lebih bipedal daripada simpanse (chimpanzé).
claims.quote: Le Koolakamba est censé être plus grand, avoir une face plus plate et une posture plus bipède que le chimpanzé.

claims.statement: The koolakamba was described as early as 1852 by Doctor Franquet in his report on the great apes of Gabon (grands Singes du Gabon).
claims.statement_id: Koolakamba sudah dideskripsikan pada 1852 oleh dokter Franquet dalam laporannya tentang kera besar Gabon (grands Singes du Gabon).
claims.quote: Le koolakamba est décrit dès 1852 par le docteur Franquet dans son rapport Notes manuscrites sur les grands Singes du Gabon

claims.statement: The animal that was shot was a full-grown male four feet three inches high.
claims.statement_id: Hewan yang ditembak itu jantan dewasa setinggi empat kaki tiga inci (four feet three inches).
claims.quote: The animal was a full-grown male four feet three inches high.

claims.statement: The kooloo-kamba's distinctive marks are a very round head, whiskers running round the face and below the chin, a round face, prominent cheek-bones and sunken cheeks.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas kooloo-kamba adalah kepala sangat bulat, cambang (whiskers) yang melingkari wajah sampai bawah dagu, wajah bulat, tulang pipi menonjol, dan pipi cekung.
claims.quote: The kooloo-kamba has for distinctive marks a very round head; whiskers running quite round the face and below the chin; the face is round; the cheek-bones prominent; the cheeks sunken

claims.statement: Its hair is black and long on the arm, though the arm was partly bare.
claims.statement_id: Rambutnya hitam (black), panjang di lengan, meski lengan itu sebagian gundul.
claims.quote: The hair is black; long on the arm, which was, however, partly bare.

claims.statement: Local people knew only that it was found more often farther interior and that, like the gorilla, it was very shy and hard to approach.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk setempat hanya tahu bahwa ia lebih sering ditemukan lebih jauh di pedalaman (farther interior) dan, seperti gorila, sangat pemalu dan sulit didekati.
claims.quote: Of its habits these people could tell me nothing, except that farther interior it was found more frequently, and that it was, like the gorilla, very shy and hard of approach.

claims.statement: According to the author, of the great apes then known the kooloo most nearly approaches man in the structure of its head.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis, di antara kera besar yang dikenal saat itu, kooloo paling mendekati manusia (approaches man) dalam struktur kepalanya.
claims.quote: The kooloo is, however, the ape, of all the great apes now known, which most nearly approaches man in the structure of its head.

claims.statement: In November 1996 a picture of an unusual ape from the Yaounde Zoo, Cameroon, was featured in the newsletter of the Internal Primate Protection League.
claims.statement_id: Pada November 1996, foto seekor kera yang tidak biasa (unusual ape) dari Kebun Binatang Yaounde, Kamerun, dimuat dalam buletin Internal Primate Protection League.
claims.quote: In November 1996, a picture of an unusual ape (taken by Peter Jenkins and Liza Gadsby at the Yaounde Zoo, Cameroon) was featured in the Newsletter of the Internal Primate Protection League (IPPL).

claims.statement: Scientifically it remains undetermined whether the Koolakamba is a chimpanzee subspecies, a gorilla-chimpanzee hybrid or simply a product of individual variation.
claims.statement_id: Secara ilmiah belum dipastikan apakah Koolakamba adalah subspesies simpanse, hibrida gorila-simpanse, atau sekadar hasil variasi individu (individual variation).
claims.quote: Scientifically, it has not been determined if the Koolakamba is a subspecies of chimpanzee, a gorilla-chimpanzee hybrid, or perhaps simply a product of individual variation.

claims.statement: The hypothesis more likely reflects the zoologists' poor understanding at the time of morphological variation (variation morphologique) in these great apes than any real hybridisation (hybridation).
claims.statement_id: Hipotesis ini lebih mungkin mencerminkan kurangnya pemahaman para zoolog masa itu tentang variasi morfologi (variation morphologique) kera besar daripada adanya hibridisasi (hybridation) nyata.
claims.quote: L'émission de cette hypothèse reflète plus vraisemblablement la méconnaissance, par les zoologistes de l'époque, de la variation morphologique inter-spécifique chez ces grands singes que l'existence d'une hybridation récente entre ces deux genres de primates.

claims.statement: Mazomba is a giant fish in the mythology of the Chaga people of Tanzania.
claims.statement_id: Mazomba adalah ikan raksasa (giant fish) dalam mitologi orang Chaga di Tanzania.
claims.quote: Mazomba is a giant fish in the mythology of the Chaga people of Tanzania.

claims.statement: Mazomba is also the name of a crater on Triton, a moon of Neptune.
claims.statement_id: Mazomba juga menjadi nama sebuah kawah (crater) di Triton, bulan Neptunus.
claims.quote: It is also the name of a crater on Triton, a moon of Neptune.

claims.statement: Mazomba is a large fish (liɗɗi mawɗi) in the lore of the Chaga people (leñol Chaga) in Tanzania (Tansani).
claims.statement_id: Mazomba adalah ikan besar (liɗɗi mawɗi) dalam kisah suku Chaga (leñol Chaga) di Tanzania (Tansani).
claims.quote: Mazomba ko liɗɗi mawɗi e nder daartol leñol Chaga to Tansani.

claims.statement: The crater name's origin: a mythical large fish from Chaga (Tanzania) tradition.
claims.statement_id: Asal nama kawah ini: ikan besar mitos (mythical large fish) dari tradisi Chaga, Tanzania.
claims.quote: Chaga (Tanzania) mythical large fish.

claims.statement: The author discusses a Chaga tale as a more meaningful version of an episode of a heartless practical joke.
claims.statement_id: Penulis membahas sebuah kisah Chaga (Chaga tale) sebagai versi yang lebih masuk akal dari sebuah episode lelucon kejam.
claims.quote: There seems no point in this beyond a senseless and heartless practical joke, but a Chaga tale

claims.statement: In the tale the leopards direct the mother to creatures called nsenzi, and they send her on to the Mazomba (large fishes), who then speak to her.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, macan tutul (leopards) menunjukkan jalan si ibu kepada makhluk nsenzi, lalu nsenzi mengarahkannya kepada Mazomba (ikan-ikan besar, large fishes) yang kemudian berbicara kepadanya.
claims.quote: The leopards directed her on to certain creatures called nsenzi (which Dr. Macdonald takes to be birds), and they to the Mazomba (Masomba? — large fishes), who said,

claims.statement: The woman is seeking the dwelling-place of Mulungu, as becomes clear later in the tale.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu sedang mencari tempat tinggal Mulungu (dwelling-place of Mulungu), sebagaimana tampak kemudian dalam kisah.
claims.quote: She does not here say that she wants to find the dwelling-place of Mulungu, but this appears later.

claims.statement: The woman is not asked to render any services to the beings she meets.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan itu tidak diminta memberi jasa (render any services) kepada makhluk-makhluk yang ditemuinya.
claims.quote: The woman is not asked to render any services to those she meets

claims.statement: When she reaches the village of Mulungu, Mulungu calls the crocodile and restores her child.
claims.statement_id: Setibanya di desa Mulungu, Mulungu memanggil buaya (crocodile) dan mengembalikan anaknya.
claims.quote: When she reaches “ the village of Mu- lungu ” and tells her story, Mulungu calls the crocodile and restores her child.

claims.statement: Her companions, hearing what had happened, at once threw their babies into the water and climbed the tree.
claims.statement_id: Teman-temannya, setelah mendengar kejadian itu, segera melempar bayi mereka ke air dan memanjat pohon (climbed the tree).
claims.quote: Her companions, when they heard what had happened, at once threw their babies into the water and climbed the tree.

claims.statement: Moussa Gname is a culture hero in epic and folk tales of the Songhai people in West Africa.
claims.statement_id: Moussa Gname adalah pahlawan budaya (culture hero) dalam kisah epik dan cerita rakyat orang Songhai di Afrika Barat (West Africa).
claims.quote: is a culture hero in epic and folklore tales of the Songhai people, in West Africa.

claims.statement: The main source for the hero is the epics collected by M. A. Dupuis Yakouba at the start of the twentieth century.
claims.statement_id: Sumber utama tentang pahlawan ini adalah epos yang dikumpulkan M. A. Dupuis Yakouba pada awal abad ke-20 (twentieth century).
claims.quote: The main source for the hero are the epics collected by M. A. Dupuis Yakouba at the start of the twentieth century.

claims.statement: Moussa's origin is mythical and, like Moses, his father is unknown; he is born of a woman who sleeps under a tree and is impregnated by the spirit dwelling in it.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul Moussa bersifat mitis; seperti Musa (Moses), ayahnya tidak diketahui. Ia lahir dari perempuan yang tertidur di bawah pohon dan dihamili roh (spirit) penghuni pohon itu.
claims.quote: Moussa's origin is mythical, and his father, like Moses unknown. He is born of a woman who falls asleep under a tree and is impregnated by a spirit that dwells in the tree.

claims.statement: A local leader, Kuruyore, sees Moussa as the future leader, but people do not believe him and Moussa is bullied by other children.
claims.statement_id: Pemimpin setempat, Kuruyore, melihat Moussa sebagai calon pemimpin, tetapi orang-orang tidak percaya, dan Moussa dirundung (bullied) anak-anak lain.
claims.quote: A local leader, Kuruyore, sees in him the future leader of their people but they don't believe him, and Moussa is bullied by the other children.

claims.statement: His mother sends him to the tree where his spirit-father teaches him hunting magic.
claims.statement_id: Ibunya menyuruhnya ke pohon tempat ayah-rohnya (spirit-father) mengajarinya sihir berburu (hunting magic).
claims.quote: Finally, he goes to his mother, who in turn sends him to the tree where his spirit-father teaches him hunting magic.

claims.statement: He accepts the position of chief on condition that nobody eats cooked food in the bush.
claims.statement_id: Ia menerima kedudukan kepala (chief) dengan syarat tak seorang pun makan makanan masak di semak belantara (bush).
claims.quote: he accepts his position as chief on the condition that none of the people will eat cooked food in the bush.

claims.statement: His greatest heroic feat, while still young, was defeating the mythical monster the Hira.
claims.statement_id: Kepahlawanan terbesarnya, saat masih muda, adalah mengalahkan monster mitos Hira.
claims.quote: His greatest heroic feat, performed while still young, was to defeat the mythical monster the Hira.

claims.statement: Mousa-Gnamé's father is a Genie (Génie); his mother was named Gnamé, a Gow and aunt of Kouarondembo.
claims.statement_id: Ayah Mousa-Gnamé adalah Genie (Génie), dan ibunya bernama Gnamé, seorang Gow, bibi Kouarondembo.
claims.quote: Mousa-Gnamé. Son père est un Génie, sa mère se nommait Gnamé, elle était gow et tante de Kouarondembo.

claims.statement: He would be called Mousa-Gnamé (after his mother's name) or Mousa-Djinni (because of his father).
claims.statement_id: Ia akan dinamai Mousa-Gnamé (dari nama ibunya) atau Mousa-Djinni (karena ayahnya).
claims.quote: On t'appellera Mousa-Gnamé (nom de sa mère) ou Mousa-Djinni (à cause de son père)

claims.statement: The Genies taught him spells (sortilèges) to fly (voler) and to turn into rain (pluie).
claims.statement_id: Para Genie mengajarinya sihir (sortilèges) untuk terbang (voler) dan untuk berubah menjadi hujan (pluie).
claims.quote: Ils lui enseignèrent des sortilèges pour voler, pour se tranformer en pluie.

claims.statement: He married Kamankiri's daughter (fille de Kamankiri) and had a daughter named Fatimata-Mousa.
claims.statement_id: Ia menikahi putri Kamankiri (fille de Kamankiri) dan mempunyai anak perempuan bernama Fatimata-Mousa.
claims.quote: Il se maria avec la fille de Kamankiri, en eut une fille nommée Fatimata-Mousa.

claims.statement: He became general chief of the Gow (chef général des Gow) after Kourouyoré resigned.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi kepala umum para Gow (chef général des Gow) setelah Kourouyoré mengundurkan diri.
claims.quote: Il devint chef général des Gow, après la démission de Kourouyoré.

claims.statement: Mousa drew his knife (couteau) and cut the Hira's throat.
claims.statement_id: Mousa mencabut pisaunya (couteau) dan menggorok Hira.
claims.quote: Mousa tira son couteau et égorgea le Hira.

claims.statement: They stayed in the village (village), and Mousa married Meynsata.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tinggal di desa (village), dan Mousa menikahi Meynsata.
claims.quote: Ils restèrent au village et Mousa épousa Meynsata.

claims.statement: In Chickasaw mythology, Panti is a fabulous beast with exceptionally lovely teeth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Chickasaw, Panti adalah hewan ajaib (fabulous beast) yang giginya luar biasa indah.
claims.quote: In Chickasaw mythology, Panti is a fabulous beast with exceptionally lovely teeth

claims.statement: Its lovely teeth will be exchanged for lost baby teeth.
claims.statement_id: Gigi indahnya akan ditukarkan dengan gigi susu (baby teeth) yang tanggal.
claims.quote: with exceptionally lovely teeth which it will exchange for lost baby teeth.

claims.statement: It is similar to creatures such as the Tooth Fairy and Ratoncito Pérez.
claims.statement_id: Panti mirip dengan makhluk seperti Peri Gigi (Tooth Fairy) dan Ratoncito Pérez.
claims.quote: It is similar to creatures like the Tooth Fairy and Ratoncito Pérez.

claims.statement: The information on Panti is referenced to the dictionary Chickasaw: An Analytical Dictionary (University of Oklahoma Press, 1994).
claims.statement_id: Keterangan tentang Panti dirujuk ke kamus Chickasaw: An Analytical Dictionary (University of Oklahoma Press, 1994).
claims.quote: Chickasaw: An Analytical Dictionary. Norman: University of Oklahoma Press, 1994.

claims.statement: Panti is likened to the Tooth Fairy (Eze Fairy) and Ratoncito Pérez.
claims.statement_id: Panti disamakan dengan Peri Gigi (Eze Fairy) dan Ratoncito Pérez.
claims.quote: Ọ dị ka Eze Fairy nke Ratoncito Pérez dere.

claims.statement: In Chickasaw folklore (akụkọ ifo Chickasaw), Panti is an animal (anụ ọhịa).
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Chickasaw (akụkọ ifo Chickasaw), Panti adalah seekor hewan (anụ ọhịa).
claims.quote: Na akụkọ ifo Chickasaw, Panti bụ anụ ọhịa

claims.statement: In Cook Islands mythology, Vaitakere is the father-in-law of Tangaroa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Kepulauan Cook (Cook Islands), Vaitakere adalah ayah mertua (father-in-law) Tangaroa.
claims.quote: In Cook Islands mythology, Vaitakere is the father-in-law of Tangaroa.

claims.statement: He discovered breadfruit in the mountains and his wife discovered the chestnut.
claims.statement_id: Ia menemukan sukun (breadfruit) di pegunungan, dan istrinya menemukan kastanye (chestnut).
claims.quote: He discovered breadfruit in the mountains and his wife discovered the chestnut.

claims.statement: He found the bread-fruit (mburu), and his wife (debbo makko) found the chestnut (kastan).
claims.statement_id: Ia menemukan buah roti (mburu), dan istrinya (debbo makko) menemukan kastanye (kastan).
claims.quote: O yiyti mburu e nder koye makko, debbo makko yiyti kastan.

claims.statement: One food was the breadfruit Vaitakere, father-in-law of Tangaroa, found growing in the mountains; the other was ii, probably the Tahitian ifi or ihi, the chestnut, found by Vaitakere's wife.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu makanan itu adalah sukun (breadfruit) yang ditemukan Vaitakere, ayah mertua Tangaroa, tumbuh di pegunungan; yang lain adalah ii, mungkin ifi atau ihi Tahiti (Tahitian), yaitu kastanye, yang ditemukan istri Vaitakere.
claims.quote: one was the breadfruit discovered growing in the mountains by Vaitakere, the father-in-law of Tangaroa, the other ii, probably the Tahitian ifi, ihi, or chestnut, discovered by Vaitakere's wife.

claims.statement: According to Polynesian traditions, two new foods were discovered in Hawaiki and the use of vari was given up.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi Polinesia (Polynesian traditions), di Hawaiki ditemukan dua makanan baru (two new foods), dan penggunaan vari ditinggalkan.
claims.quote: in Polynesian traditions it was in Hawaiki ... two new foods were discovered, and the use of vari

claims.statement: These islanders, in one of their traditions, call vari the food of the people when they lived in Atia.
claims.statement_id: Para penduduk pulau itu (Rarotonga) dalam salah satu tradisinya menyebut vari sebagai makanan orang-orang ketika masih tinggal di Atia.
claims.quote: And these islanders in one of their traditions make vari the name of the food of the people when living in Atia.

claims.statement: This tradition is given in the karakias of the Rarotongans.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi ini disebut dalam karakia (mantra/doa) orang Rarotonga (Rarotongans).
claims.quote: as it is put in the karakias of the Rarotongans.

claims.statement: Their alternative name Bakhna Rakhna literally means good people.
claims.statement_id: Nama lain mereka, Bakhna Rakhna, secara harfiah berarti orang baik (good people).
claims.quote: Their alternatively used name Bakhna Rakhna literally means good people.

claims.statement: Yumboes are spirits of the dead and, like many supernatural beings in African beliefs, are entirely pearly-white.
claims.statement_id: Yumboes adalah roh orang mati (spirits of the dead) dan, seperti banyak makhluk gaib dalam kepercayaan Afrika (African), seluruhnya berwarna putih mutiara.
claims.quote: Yumboes are the spirits of the dead and, like many supernatural beings in African beliefs, they are completely of a pearly-white colour.

claims.statement: They are sometimes said to have silver hair.
claims.statement_id: Kadang dikatakan mereka berambut perak (silver hair).
claims.quote: They are sometimes said to have silver hair.

claims.statement: The only known source for yumboe legends is Thomas Keightley's book The Fairy Mythology.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya sumber legenda yumboes yang diketahui adalah buku Thomas Keightley, The Fairy Mythology.
claims.quote: The only known source for legends on yumboes is Thomas Keightley's book The Fairy Mythology.

claims.statement: Keightley got his account from a woman who as a child lived on Goree Island off Senegal and heard of the yumboes from a Wolof maid.
claims.statement_id: Keightley mendapat ceritanya dari seorang perempuan yang semasa kecil tinggal di Pulau Goree, lepas pantai Senegal, yang mendengar tentang yumboes dari pelayan Wolof.
claims.quote: Keightley received his account from a woman who had lived on Goree Island, off the coast of Senegal, when she was a child. She had heard about the yumboes from a Wolof maid.

claims.statement: They also resemble ancestral ghosts described in many African countries.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga mirip arwah leluhur (ancestral ghosts) yang digambarkan di banyak negara Afrika.
claims.quote: They also bear a resemblance to ancestral ghosts described in many African countries.

claims.statement: Yumboes appear as helpful fairies in the 2021 novel Skin of the Sea by Nigerian Welsh writer Natasha Bowen.
claims.statement_id: Yumboes muncul sebagai peri penolong dalam novel Skin of the Sea (2021) karya Natasha Bowen, penulis Nigeria-Wales (Nigerian Welsh).
claims.quote: Yumboes appear as helpful fairies in the 2021 novel Skin of the Sea by Nigerian Welsh writer Natasha Bowen.

claims.statement: The Jaloff people of the African mainland opposite Goree believe in beings strikingly similar to the Gothic fairies.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk Jaloff di daratan Afrika (Africa), di seberang Pulau Goree, percaya pada sejenis makhluk yang sangat mirip dengan peri Gotik (Gothic Fairies).
claims.quote: The Jaloff inhabitants of the mainland of Africa, opposite the isle of Goree, believe in a species of beings who have a striking and surprising correspondence with the Gothic Fairies.

claims.statement: They call them Yumboes and describe them as about two feet high and white, as all preternatural things are in Africa.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menyebutnya Yumboes dan menggambarkannya setinggi sekitar dua kaki (two feet) serta berwarna putih, seperti segala yang gaib di Afrika (Africa).
claims.quote: They call them Yumboes, and describe them as being about two feet high, of a white colour, as every thing preternatural is in Africa.

claims.statement: The Africans call the Yumboes Bakhna Rakhna, or Good People.
claims.statement_id: Orang Afrika (Africans) menyebut Yumboes sebagai Bakhna Rakhna, atau orang baik (Good People).
claims.quote: the Africans call the Yumboes, Bakhna Rakhna, or Good People.

claims.statement: The dress of the Yumboes matches that of the natives exactly, and they imitate their actions in every particular.
claims.statement_id: Pakaian Yumboes persis sama dengan pakaian penduduk setempat (natives), dan mereka meniru tindakan penduduk dalam segala hal.
claims.quote: the Yumboes exactly corresponds with that of the natives, and they imitate their actions in every particular.

claims.statement: They attach themselves to particular families; when a member dies, the Yumboes are heard lamenting and dancing on the graves.
claims.statement_id: Mereka melekat pada keluarga tertentu; bila anggota keluarga itu meninggal, Yumboes terdengar meratapinya dan menari di atas kuburnya (graves).
claims.quote: They attach themselves to particular families; and whenever any of their members die, the Yumboes are heard to lament them, and to dance upon their graves.

claims.statement: The Moors believe the Yumboes are the souls of their deceased friends.
claims.statement_id: Orang Moor (Moors) percaya Yumboes adalah jiwa sahabat mereka yang telah meninggal.
claims.quote: The Moors believe the Yumboes to be the souls of their deceased friends.

claims.statement: The Yumboes' chief abode is an underground dwelling on the Paps, hills about three miles from the coast.
claims.statement_id: Tempat tinggal utama Yumboes adalah hunian bawah tanah di Paps, perbukitan (hills) sekitar tiga mil (three miles) dari pantai.
claims.quote: The chief abode of the Yumboes is a subterraneous dwelling on the Paps, the hills about three miles distant from the coast.

claims.statement: There nothing but hands and feet could be seen, laying and removing the dishes.
claims.statement_id: Di sana yang terlihat hanya tangan dan kaki (hands and feet) yang menata dan mengangkat hidangan.
claims.quote: how nothing but hands and feet were to be seen, which laid and removed the various dishes

claims.statement: They creep to the huts where the women are pounding coos-coos, or corn, in mortars.
claims.statement_id: Mereka mengendap ke gubuk tempat para perempuan menumbuk coos-coos atau jagung (corn) di lesung.
claims.quote: They steal to the huts, where the women are pounding in mortars the coos-coos, or corn,

claims.statement: They are also seen at night in their canoes, fishing in the bay.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga terlihat pada malam hari (at night) di kano, menangkap ikan di teluk.
claims.quote: They are also seen at night in their canoes, out fishing in the bay.

claims.statement: They bury palm-wine, drink it when sour until drunk, and then make a great noise beating Jaloff drums on the hills.
claims.statement_id: Mereka mengubur tuak sawit (palm-wine), meminumnya setelah masam sampai mabuk, lalu membuat keributan dengan menabuh genderang Jaloff di perbukitan.
claims.quote: They bury palm-wine, and when it becomes sour they drink of it till it intoxicates them, and then make a great noise, beating Jaloff drums on the hills.

claims.statement: Their name Bakhna Rakhna means good people (yimɓe moƴƴuɓe).
claims.statement_id: Nama yang mereka pakai, Bakhna Rakhna, berarti orang-orang baik (yimɓe moƴƴuɓe).
claims.quote: Innde maɓɓe nde ɓe kuutortoo nde Bakhna Rakhna firti ko yimɓe moƴƴuɓe.
